541540|2026-09.headline: Solara Q2 FY27 revenue rose 33% YoY to INR 418 crore and EBITDA more than doubled to INR 77 crore, with PAT of INR 28.5 crore.
541540|2026-09.overview: Management called Q2 FY27 its best quarter in about five years, with growth across revenue, gross margin, EBITDA and PAT despite West Asia-driven raw material and pricing pressures. The base business grew 37% YoY to INR 327 crore at a 23.6% EBITDA margin, while Ibuprofen came close to breakeven at a INR 91 crore revenue base. Net debt fell to about INR 500 crore from INR 614 crore at March 2026, helped by about INR 100 crore of rights issue proceeds, though it rose about INR 20 crore QoQ on working capital. The Ibuprofen strategic review has been extended by a further 12 weeks, with no decision yet.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of ~INR 10 crore YoY; ~75% higher QoQ
+37% YoY; above INR 300 crore for third straight quarter
vs roughly breakeven in H1 FY26

segments.name: Base business (API)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 327 crore (+37% YoY), EBITDA INR 77 crore at 23.6% margin; gross margin about 50%, below the 52-55% historical range due to mix and input costs. Regulated markets about 78% of revenue.

segments.name: Ibuprofen
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 91 crore (+21% YoY, +18% QoQ) on better prices and volumes; EBITDA loss narrowed to near breakeven from ~INR 9 crore loss in Q1 and ~21% loss margin two quarters earlier. Management calls the market commodity-like and the gain temporary.

segments.name: CRAMS
segments.commentary: Described as very small within the overall business; management is marketing services and chemistry to customers, with focus deferred to the core business.

guidance_outlook: Ibuprofen strategic review to conclude in about 12 weeks; options remain repurposing the plant into a multiproduct facility (including captive intermediates) or finding an external buyer.
Management is 'cautiously optimistic' and says a turnaround qualifies after two more quarters at or above Q2 levels.
Base business gross margin: management sees 52-55% as sustainable; adjusted for unrecovered raw material costs, reported ~50.5% would be ~53%+.
Cost base expected to stay flat, within plus or minus 2-3%, so incremental gross margin should flow to EBITDA.
Five DMF filings targeted for FY27: one in Q1, one in Q2, and three more by March 2027.
Capex commitment of INR 40-50 crore per year; net debt/EBITDA expected to stay in a similar range (~1.8x) over the medium term.
capex_capacity: Capex run-rate about INR 10-15 crore per quarter, within an annual commitment of INR 40-50 crore.
Vizag facility is mothballed with no current manufacturing; idle Ibuprofen-related equipment in CWIP sold for INR 4.5 crore.
Mangalore facility passed an ANVISA audit in August 2026; Cuddalore passed one in May 2026.
Debottlenecking and capex for high-margin products are planned to add capacity and lift EBITDA.
demand_pricing: Customers agreed to price increases; pass-through was about INR 25 crore in base business and INR 10-12 crore in Ibuprofen, so about INR 25-30 crore of the INR 418 crore revenue came from price and the rest from volume.

Base business gross margin was held back by raw material and solvent cost increases tied to the West Asia crisis; full pass-through is not achieved with every customer or product, and management expects this for one to two more quarters.
Ibuprofen demand rose this quarter; management says capacity additions in India and closures in the West may affect supply, and Ibuprofen is a commodity-pricing market.
KSM sourcing: about 60-70% India, 20-25% China, balance Europe. Container shipping delays pushed shipment lead times from 2-3 days to 5-7 days, lifting receivables at quarter end.
Strides (related party) contributed about 25% of business on average, rising to 30-35% in some quarters; INR 328 crore in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Vizag INR 4.5 crore exceptional item a one-off or the start of a wider reassessment of the INR 182 crore Vizag project?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a one-off sale of idle Ibuprofen-related equipment in CWIP; no further Vizag charges are foreseen for now, pending the review.

qa_highlights.question: Trade receivables have risen more than fourfold YoY; what is driving this?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a ~50% rise in revenue, quarter-end billing concentration (last 7-10 days) and container shortages stretching billing-to-shipment from 2-3 days to 5-7 days; no payment terms were changed.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the net debt increase was from capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex was about INR 10-15 crore per quarter; the rest was inventory build of about INR 20 crore to secure raw material.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin definition, and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the accounting methodology is unchanged and it will take the input on board; base business GM is comfortable in the 52-55% range, and reported 50.5% would be ~53%+ after unrecovered raw material costs.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Ibuprofen business be profitable in the current quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot predict; Q2 breakeven depended on macro conditions and price increases, and it is hard to hold the same result in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Vizag plant being sold, and are customers offering more volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Vizag is mothballed; management says it has not announced a sale and that strategic options cover CRAMS, Vizag and Ibuprofen, with a decision after the 12-week review.

risks_watch: Ibuprofen review outcome (sale or repurposing) due in about 12 weeks; management has already deferred the timeline once.
Receivables and working capital: trade receivables up more than fourfold YoY and rising inventory tie up cash; net debt rose QoQ.
Gross margin dependence on the West Asia crisis, solvent and raw material costs; Ibuprofen results may reverse if supply normalises, which the analyst asked about.

541556|2026-03.headline: RITES ends FY26 with record INR 9,416 crore order book; export income recovers to ~INR 300 crore, but management says FY27 profit records are unlikely.
541556|2026-03.overview: Management said FY26 was in line with its roadmap, targeting double-digit growth with margins held. Q4 execution was about INR 750+ crore and the order book reached an all-time high of INR 9,416 crore on 31 March 2026, with over 50% of it 12-18 months old. Export income recovered to about INR 300 crore after nearly two years of decline, with a balance export order of about INR 1,750 crore led by 200 Bangladesh coaches. Management guided that revenue may hit an all-time high in FY27, but PAT and EBITDA records are not expected until at least two to three years out because of lower-margin turnkey mix.

financial_highlights.change: First increase after nearly two years

segments.name: Consultancy
segments.commentary: Consultancy revenue of INR 1,185 crore rose 6% YoY across 13 verticals, with 700+ live consultancy orders. Quality assurance revenue grew 16% and is back to FY24 levels, with non-IR share now about 60%+.

segments.name: Turnkey
segments.commentary: Turnkey revenue fell by about INR 200 crore YoY. Turnkey order book of INR 4,580 crore is about two-thirds young (1-2 years), and management expects it to contribute more from FY27 at lower margins.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue of about INR 300 crore in FY26 came from 10 Mozambique locomotives. Bangladesh 200-coach order: first rake of 20 coaches due in about two months; prototypes approved.

segments.name: REMCL (leasing/power purchase consultancy)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR 163 crore (up 16%), profit about INR 90 crore (up 19%), dividend about INR 42 crore. Growth limited to IR traffic volumes; new renewable and international consultancy orders being pursued.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for an all-time high revenue in FY27 but not an all-time high PAT or EBITDA; profit records may take two to three more years.
Profits will grow in FY27, though no number was given.
Management said PAT margin of 15% and EBITDA margin of 20% will not be breached, by monitoring high-margin orders.
Export execution in FY27 is expected to be well above INR 300 crore; a clearer figure is expected at end of Q1 FY27.
High dividend payout ratio to continue.
capex_capacity: Bangladesh: 200 coaches in 10 rakes of 20; first rake targeted in about two months, with rakes at least three to four rakes apart in FY27 and production rate to step up after first delivery.
Converting spare Indian Railways diesel locomotives to Cape Gauge for African export: prototypes ready, first two units expected in coming months, with an order for about 30 in-service locomotives.
Electrification of Indian Railways is near 100%, so REMCL power-purchase consultancy growth is tied to traffic volumes.
demand_pricing: Order inflow run-rate is about one order a day and one export order a quarter; over 70% of fresh inflow is competitive, and 63% of the total order book is competitive.
Management said margins on new orders are much lower, so mix shift will pressure margins as new orders convert.

Turnkey fee economics: a 5% consultancy fee on a INR 100 crore project equals INR 5 crore; under turnkey the contract value is INR 105 crore but the scope and revenue are unchanged, so margins are lower.
Management sees no major impact from fuel or raw material costs because most contractor contracts have price variation clauses; travel costs are the main cost to watch.
Recent wins include an airport consultancy order and a Kandla shipbuilding cluster order; management sees no drop in strike rate despite budget capex concerns.

qa_highlights.question: Why is management optimistic on disruptive growth given geopolitical headwinds, and can margins be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book has risen over the last 7-8 quarters, with over 50% of it 12-18 months old and set to convert in FY27. Margins on new orders are lower, so margins will dilute as they convert, but PAT of 15% and EBITDA of 20% will be defended.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise and will they stay high?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher expenses came from logistics for moving the 10 Mozambique locomotives (six moved in Q4) and warranty provisions tied to export execution. FY27 will see a slight increase, partly offset by lower logistics costs on rail-moved Bangladesh coaches.

qa_highlights.question: How much export revenue can come in FY27 from the INR 1,700+ crore balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is aiming well above INR 300 crore but cannot give a firm number yet; a clearer figure is expected at end of Q1 FY27 once the first rake moves.

qa_highlights.question: When will turnkey revenue recover to last year's level?
qa_highlights.answer: Turnkey revenue was about INR 200 crore lower YoY. Turnkey order book of INR 4,580 crore is about two-thirds young, and management expects it to reach last year's turnkey revenue levels as IIT/IIM building and rail siding projects start generating revenue in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will the government capex cut delay railway contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no major impact on consultancy from fresh orders or milestone progress, citing recent wins across railways, PSUs, ports, highways and airports.

541556|2026-06.headline: RITES Q1 FY27 revenue grew 9-10% YoY, PAT about 8%; order book at INR 9,450 crore, with export revenue slipping into Q2 on Bangladesh first rake.

Export revenue from the Bangladesh coach order was not recognised in Q1 because the first rake (about 20 coaches, four coach types) was still being finalised; dispatch is expected within about 10 days, with recognition in Q2. Consolidated EBITDA margin was 22% and PAT margin about 17%, both held sequentially, and management reiterated red lines of 20% EBITDA and 15% PAT margin. Order book reached INR 9,450 crore after 128 fresh orders worth INR 670 crore, with about 70% of fresh orders won competitively.

541557|2026-03.headline: Fine Organic FY26 consolidated revenue rose 4.3% to INR 2,365 crore and PAT 1.6% to INR 417 crore; management guides flat growth until SEZ commissioning in 2H FY28.
541557|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue grew 4.3% to INR 2,365 crore from INR 2,269 crore, with PAT up 1.6% to INR 417 crore and EBITDA margin at 20.4%. Management said all plants run at near full utilisation, so volume growth is capped until the JNPA SEZ plant and US plant come on line. The company approved acquiring up to 80% of Oleofine Organics BHD, Malaysia (cash consideration about INR 82.9 crore), and continued capex in SEZ, US, Dubai and Thailand. Raw material and freight costs rose in Q4 on the West Asia conflict, and management expects vegetable-oil prices to stay high through FY27.

541729|2026-03.headline: HDFC AMC FY26 profit after tax rose 16% to INR28.6 billion; QAAUM grew 20% to INR9.3 trillion and dividend of INR54 per share was recommended.
541729|2026-03.overview: HDFC AMC closed FY26 with revenue from operations of INR41.2 billion (up 18% YoY), operating profit of INR32.1 billion (up 18%, 35 bps of AUM) and PAT of INR28.6 billion (up 16%). QAAUM reached INR9.3 trillion (up 20%), with equity-oriented AUM at INR6 trillion and unique investors up 3.5 million to 16.7 million. Management highlighted record March 2026 SIP flows of INR321 billion industry-wide and said investor behaviour during the market correction was disciplined. The major open issue is the SEBI base expense ratio (BER) change effective April 1, 2026, which management expects to offset through commission changes with no material P&L impact.

segments.name: Equity-oriented funds
segments.commentary: Equity-oriented AUM reached INR6 trillion. Actively managed equity yield was about 60-61 bps, versus 56 bps including index funds.

segments.name: Debt and liquid funds
segments.commentary: Debt yield was 28 bps and liquid 13 bps in Q4. Management said the balance sheet debt book is run with modest duration and largely passive management.

segments.name: Alternatives, PMS and international
segments.commentary: Alternatives margins are marginally above equity margins, and discretionary PMS is in line with equity margins. Non-discretionary EPFO/SPFO mandates earn thinner net economics. GIFT City has five live funds, all wholly owned.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the gross impact of the base expense ratio change on existing book at about 3-4 bps, to be largely offset by commission restructuring and cost management, so targeted P&L impact is not material.
The 5 bps trail previously paid in lieu of exit load has been removed, and GST on management fees now sits outside the expense ratio, requiring margin adjustments.

No formal cost guidance is given. Employee cost ex-ESOP grew about 12.5% YoY, with five-year CAGRs of about 13% for employee cost and 13.5% for non-employee cost; costs are expected to grow broadly in line with business.
Management said flow market share is above book market share, and the company will launch SIF products only after careful design, not as a race.
Management said the SEBI-classified category presence is complete and new launches will be selective, with focus on sharpening existing funds.
capex_capacity: Physical branch network significantly expanded over the last couple of years, with further expansion under evaluation.
Investment in AI, cloud technology, cybersecurity and talent for PMS, international and alternatives; management called these foundational investments.
Rajan Anandan (Peak XV) appointed as invitee and external expert on the Technology Committee for a three-year term.
Seven new schemes launched in FY26, and first close of a private credit fund with IFC as partner and anchor investor announced.
Two EPFO/SPFO fixed income PMS mandates won. SPFO is already being managed, and the EPFO agreement is being signed.
demand_pricing: Industry: FY26 net inflows INR7.4 trillion, with equity-oriented funds about INR4.9 trillion; March 2026 SIP collections INR321 billion (up 24% YoY, 97 million contributing accounts). Industry market share is around 12.8-13% for the last eight to nine quarters.
HDFC AMC: direct plans about 31% of equity AUM; 97% of transactions digital; total accounts above 30 million; unique investors 16.7 million, up 3.5 million, versus industry addition of 7.2 million.
Unique investor penetration rose from 17.6% (March 2023) to 27% (March 2026). Folios rose from 2.3 crore to 3 crore, and SIP and STP flows were INR48.8 billion in March 2026 (up 33% YoY).

Management said flow share is higher than book share across channels, including fintech and HDFC Securities. HDFC Bank share of the distribution pie is declining, which management attributed to broad-based growth across other channels.
Competitive pressure: management stated SBI is almost closed-architecture, and some banks are more guided in retail distribution.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the new TER/BER regulation and how will distribution commissions change?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross impact on the existing book is about 3-4 bps, to be offset through commission optimisation and cost management, so no material P&L impact is targeted. New commission structures already reflect removal of the 5 bps exit-load trail, and the company will share more detail over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why does a third-party calculation show Q4 flow market share below Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the calculation missed IDCW (dividend) payouts in Q4 that were recorded as redemptions; the company does not accept the computed figure. Management said overall flow share remains above book share.

qa_highlights.question: Why has one-year scheme performance and industry ranking weakened?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the funds remain in the top two quartiles across most categories and that many are rated 4 or 5 stars by Value Research. It pointed to long-term alpha track records, with 12-13 funds having 15-year-plus records.

qa_highlights.question: Are FY27 and FY28 expense growth targets available?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific guidance is given. Employee and non-employee costs have grown at about 13% CAGR over five years and are expected to grow in line with business and investments.

qa_highlights.question: What was the reason for the other income increase, and how is the balance sheet positioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said balance sheet equity is mainly SEBI skin-in-the-game MF holdings, which saw drawdowns in Q4. The remainder is in liquid and debt funds with modest duration and passive management.

qa_highlights.question: Will HDFC AMC launch new NFOs or SIF products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has secured all regulatory approvals for SIF. It is designing a couple of differentiated products but views the category as strategic rather than immediate. Management will stay selective on new launches.

risks_watch: SEBI base expense ratio change from April 1, 2026: margin effect depends on commission restructuring, and management said the impact is not yet quantified precisely.
Sustainability of flows if markets stay weak for longer; management cautioned that investor behaviour has not been tested over an extended downturn.
HDFC Bank channel share is declining, and management said the bank remains open architecture, with event-driven flow variability.
Rising costs from talent, technology and AI investments versus margin targets, with no formal cost guidance.
Alternatives and PMS economics are thinner for non-discretionary government mandates (EPFO/SPFO), and SIF launch timing is undefined.
Mark-to-market exposure on the SEBI skin-in-the-game equity holdings on the balance sheet.
541729|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on flows, investor maturity and long-term growth, but defensive on market share, the HDFC Bank channel and performance ranking. Management was cautious and non-committal on cost guidance, SIF timing and the quantified TER impact, saying it is still early.
key_quotes: And that clearly shows a very mature behaviour of investors.
So overall, the targeted impact on our P&L should not be material.
So overall flows are higher than the book share, that much I can tell you.
Real question is, how do we participate in a way that is consistent with our philosophy?

541729|2026-06.headline: HDFC AMC Q1 FY27: quarterly average AUM INR9.35 trillion (+13% YoY), PAT INR8.4 billion (+12% YoY), with debt AUM weakening.
541729|2026-06.overview: Quarterly average AUM reached INR9.35 trillion, up 13% YoY, with market share of 11.2% (12.4% ex-ETFs). Revenue from operations rose 14% YoY to INR11 billion and PAT rose 12% YoY to INR8.4 billion. Management said margins were maintained despite a regime change from TER to BER accounting, the removal of the 5 bps exit-load-linked charge, and brokerage rationalisation from 1 April 2026. Debt QAAUM fell and debt market share was under pressure, while SIP and systematic flows kept growing.

vs INR2.1 billion in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Equity
segments.commentary: Equity-oriented QAAUM is 65.7% of company AUM vs 56.6% for the industry; blended equity yield 58 bps. Equity market share held at around 12.8% YoY.

segments.name: Debt
segments.commentary: Debt QAAUM INR1.66 trillion with 12.9% market share; debt AUM fell about 6% QoQ on closing basis per analyst, with industry debt outflows of INR757 billion. Debt yield 28 bps.

segments.name: Liquid
segments.commentary: Liquid QAAUM INR851 billion with 10.7% market share; liquid yield 13 bps. Industry liquid inflows INR984 billion in the quarter.

segments.name: Alternatives / PMS / AIF
segments.commentary: Total alternatives AUM INR148 billion vs INR60 billion a year ago. Management says alternatives economics are slightly better than mutual fund equity; a private credit fund closes this quarter and a VC/PE fund of funds was approved with a proposed $50 million seed commitment.

guidance_outlook: Management said margins have been maintained through the new TER-to-BER regime, offset by commission optimisation and cost control; it asked not to read too much into quarterly yield movements.
Net operating margin to stay within the 33-35 bps of AUM corridor, per CFO; management will not underinvest.
Non-cash ESOP cost guided at INR79-80 crore for FY27, INR63 crore for FY28, INR41 crore for FY29 and INR11 crore for FY30.
Company declined to forecast AUM growth. Buyback vs dividend is a Board decision.

Investment team: 37 investment professionals on mutual fund side; 6 on PE/VC, 6 on private credit, 8 on PMS (debt and equity).
demand_pricing: Industry SIP contributions INR318 billion in June 2026 vs INR273 billion in June 2025 (+17%); folios 279 million; unique investors 61.9 million.

Debt fund outflows attributed to rupee and rate volatility, crude and geopolitics; management said industry must make debt funds more attractive to retail.
Distributor economics described as a long-term partnership; management said manufacturer-distributor economics do not change with market conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debt AUM fall about 6% QoQ and why are debt outflows strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said investors redeemed debt funds on rupee, rate and crude volatility while liquid funds saw inflows; HDFC AMC has a decent share of both moves.

qa_highlights.question: Is the yield uptick from product mix or the TER/BER change, and what is the PMS/AIF contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not read too much into early-quarter movement post the accounting change. Alternatives earn 80-90 bps management fee; PMS discretionary book is in line with equity margins, non-discretionary is very tight economics.

qa_highlights.question: Has the distribution commission been rationalised and will revenue yield benefit in later quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Changes from 1 April 2026: removal of 5 bps extra TER charged in lieu of exit load, shift from TER to BER plus statutory levies, and brokerage rationalisation. Offset through commission optimisation and cost control; margins maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ESOP cost jump, and is FY27 guidance unchanged?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 cost of about INR23 crore reflects a June 2025 grant under the new plan; FY27 non-cash ESOP cost guided at INR79-80 crore, unchanged at INR67 crore level per analyst reference point is for prior guide. Management said costs should be viewed annually.

qa_highlights.question: Was there an operating cost growth guidance of 12-13% ex non-cash?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said to focus on the 33-35 bps net operating margin corridor rather than quarterly cost trends.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the performance improvement in June?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited top-two-quartile performance over 2 and 3 years on AUM-weighted basis; Balance Advantage Fund in Q1 over 3, 5, 10 years, and Flexicap in Q1 over 2, 3, 5, 10 years.

risks_watch: Debt AUM outflows and debt market share pressure; management said it needs to make debt funds more attractive to retail.
Sustainability of SIP momentum and first-time investor behaviour through an extended market downturn, which management said has not yet been tested.
Distributor-channel share shifts toward fintechs; bank share fell to 9.6% from 10.4%.
Operating cost growth and rising non-cash ESOP cost; management said it will not underinvest.
Yield trajectory under the new TER-to-BER regime; management did not give forward yield guidance.

541729|2026-09.headline: HDFC AMC Q2 FY27: revenue from operations up 14% YoY to INR11.7 billion; operating profit up 16% to INR9.1 billion at 36 bps of AUM.

Reported PAT is not comparable YoY because the year-ago quarter had a INR468 million tax provision reversal. Management pushed alternatives, PMS and GIFT City as growth areas, and defended cost growth as a mix of routine costs and forward investment.

segments.name: Liquid

segments.name: Alternatives and PMS

EPFO fixed income mandate went live this quarter; management says AIF fees run 80-90 bps above equity MF fees. Share of non-MF revenue described as small.

segments.name: Passive and GIFT City

541741|2026-03.headline: Fratelli Q4 FY26 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR36 crores and EBITDA turned near breakeven at INR1.06 crores for FY26, with FY27 guidance of about 30% growth.

541770|2026-09.headline: CreditAccess Grameen posted record Q2 FY27 PAT of INR 502 Crore, raised FY27 ROA guidance to 5.2%-5.8% and ROE to 21%-24%.
541770|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 PAT hit a record INR 502 Crore and H1 PAT reached INR 995 Crore versus INR 778 Crore in H1 FY26, with H1 ROA at 5.9% and ROE at 23.8%. AUM grew 19.5% YoY to INR 30,946 Crore, while the Group Loan book declined 2% since the start of FY27 due to write-offs and graduation. Asset quality improved sequentially (GNPA 1.79%, NNPA 0.59%), but management flagged a rise in PAR accretion in August-September from floods and festivities and early drought stress in about 6 Maharashtra districts. Management raised FY27 profitability guidance and cut its NIM guidance sharply upward, while passing a 50 bps lending rate cut from October.

segments.name: Group Loans
segments.commentary: Book at INR 23,746 Crore as of September 2026, down 2% from start of FY27 due to write-offs and graduation; INR 614 Crore written off in H1 mostly from Group Loans. Management expects return to guided growth in H2.

segments.name: Retail Finance
segments.commentary: AUM INR 7,200 Crore, 23.3% of total AUM (20.6% in Q1 FY27). Secured book (secured business loans, affordable housing, 2-wheeler) grew 60.9% YoY to INR 695 Crore; 2-wheeler book crossed INR 60 Crore from INR 20 Crore in Q1.

segments.name: Mortgage
segments.commentary: Operates from 428 branches per Q&A, up from 120 earlier; management says NPAs rising but within tolerance, budgeting about 2% credit cost in mortgage.

segments.name: Individual Business Loans
segments.commentary: Graduation product (Unnati average tenure over 7 years, average credit score above 730); PAR 30 has not crossed 3% even at the peak of the credit cycle.

guidance_outlook: FY27 ROA guidance raised to 5.2%-5.8% from 4%-4.8%; ROE raised to 21%-24% from 16%-20%.
FY27 NIM guidance of 14.4%-14.7%, up from 12.8%-13.2% earlier, after factoring a 50 bps lending rate cut from October.
AUM growth guidance of 20%-25% retained; Microfinance seen range-bound at 10%-12% growth while retail grows faster.

Credit cost guidance of 3%-4% maintained; H1 run-rate about 3%, Q3 expected to inch up, with ECL provisioning rising 5-6 bps per quarter in Q3 and Q4. Management said credit cost likely 3.5%-4% for FY27.

Insurance commission regulation could reduce ROA by 25-30 bps; management says pricing could offset it.

Industry: banks have significantly pulled back from microfinance, while MFIs and NBFCs gained share; management sees no broad pullback by large players.
Gold loan exposure stable at about 10-12% of overall customer base.
Lending rate cut of 50 bps across products except mortgage and 2-wheeler; the company is among the lowest-priced lenders in microfinance.
Drought-related requests for time or restructuring seen in about 6 central Maharashtra districts; no on-ground impact seen elsewhere in October.

qa_highlights.question: Why cut lending rates by 50 bps now when marginal borrowing cost rose 25-30 bps QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NIMs are at highest levels and the cut follows the pricing policy; borrowing cost is expected at 9.2%-9.3% through March as ECB refinancing replaces higher-cost debt. Risk-adjusted NIM is about 11%, with a target of 10%.

qa_highlights.question: How will credit cost trend in Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q3 to inch up; even a 5% H2 run-rate would keep FY27 within 4%. Management guided FY27 credit cost to 3.5%-4%.

qa_highlights.question: Are flood and PAR accretion spikes in UP, Bihar, MP and Tamil Nadu continuing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said September spikes were due to floods and festivities; October was normal everywhere except Maharashtra. Credit cost spike beyond 5% is the pricing threshold.

qa_highlights.question: How much exposure is in drought-affected districts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 6 central Maharashtra districts are affected, but portfolio share was not available and would be provided offline.

qa_highlights.question: Is a guarantee scheme in place for microfinance?
qa_highlights.answer: No microfinance guarantee yet; CGFMU application pending budget approval, expected to open in a week or two. Premium about 1.3%-1.5% annually covering about 75% of losses. Smaller CGTMSE and BII guarantees exist for individual lending.

qa_highlights.question: Why is borrower growth in single digits and what is the customer acquisition plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said write-offs and attrition held the count down; customer acquisition expected to show improvement in Q3 and Q4. Management targets over 1 lakh customers per month, versus about 80,000 now.

Group Loan book recovery and customer acquisition pace; borrower count growth remains weak.

Promoter-level strategic investor discussions at holding level, timing undefined.

541929|2026-03.headline: Synergy Green guides FY27 revenue to about ₹500 crore (+33%) with PBDIT margin up over 300 bps, while FY26 PBDIT margin fell to 13.10%.
541929|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was ₹123.45 crore with PBDIT of ₹14.83 crore (12.01% margin); FY26 total income was ₹376 crore (+3.5% YoY) with PBDIT of ₹48.67 crore (13.10%). Management attributed the weak year to brownfield expansion delays, outsourcing and relocation costs, and early West Asia-linked commodity and energy inflation. Capacity was expanded from 30,000 to 45,000 TPA foundry and a 20,000 TPA machining plant was added, but ramp-up is slow with utilisation expected to reach 80-90% only over 4-5 months. Management guided to ₹500-530 crore revenue and debt of ₹175-180 crore at FY27 end.

financial_highlights.change: PBDIT down ~8% in absolute terms YoY

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 FY26 sales volume (per analyst's question, management confirmed sales ~8,500 MT)

segments.commentary: Management described five revenue streams but gave no segment-wise revenue split. Export realisations were lower in FY26 due to discounted pricing linked to in-house machining under development; exports are ~25-30% of revenue and are on FOB basis.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at ~₹500 crore (~33% growth); management said the order book points to ₹530-550 crore, with 500-530 as the realistic range.
FY27 PBDIT margin expansion of over 300 bps YoY (implies ~16-16.5% per analyst's read); each ~₹30 crore of extra revenue above ₹500 crore could add ~100 bps as overheads are covered.
Export revenue expected stable at ~25-30% of revenue; revenue split ~45% H1 and ~55% H2 in FY27.
FY28 utilisation of 90%+ is possible; management views 15-20% CAGR as the medium-term target and sees ~10-15% headroom growth in FY28 from existing capacity.

Debt expected at ₹175-180 crore at end FY27 (from ~₹165 crore), with debt-to-equity below 1.5 at peak; management expects a balance-sheet improvement later, with debt possibly falling to ₹70-100 crore.
capex_capacity: Foundry expanded from 30,000 to 45,000 TPA (brownfield); max casting weight raised from 23 to 30 MT, enabling up to 5 MW turbines.

New 20,000 TPA machining and coating plant near foundry; 5th and 6th machines to be commissioned in 2-3 weeks; 3-4 machines stabilised at ~50% utilisation; machining product development 30-40% complete.

FY26 capex of ~₹250 crore (foundry expansion and machining), funded through internal accruals, equity and debt in a ~1:1 to 1:1.2 debt-equity mix. Cost of a greenfield project was earlier estimated at ₹500-600 crore, now to be reassessed in Q2-Q3 FY27.

Land acquisition of ~15-16 acres near existing site targeted within 6-9 months; cost ~₹25 crore, funded from internal accruals. Big capex expected from FY28; commissioning of a new unit ~15 months from initiation.
10 MW solar captive capacity onboarded from October 2025; management noted some lapsed units due to a banking-policy dispute with the state electricity board.
demand_pricing: Utilisation: FY26 utilisation on the 30,000 MT base was 93%; the current month is running near 2,500 MT (about 230,000 MT annualised per management wording) with management guiding 80-90% on the expanded base over 4-5 months.
Product mix: 12 new product developments in FY26; complexity has risen versus the earlier 2-4 products for two OEMs, which is slowing ramp-up.

Customers: six of the 15 leading global OEMs; includes Vestas, Siemens Gamesa, Senvion, Adani, Envision, GE, Nordex, Flender, ZF; non-wind adds Terex, Millikron, Willow, Mahindra, L&T; L&T order for a super thermal power component and BHEL in discussion (30-40 MT casings currently imported).

Pricing: quarterly indexation for pig iron, billet and CRC; other elements reset annually. Management cited a ~₹140/kg-type realisation relation (₹135-140 per the call); a Vestas contract for Jan-Dec 2027 is near finalisation with ~30-40% growth.

Competition: only one Chinese OEM (Envision) is active; management says new entrants need 3-5 years. Yuan appreciation (~20%) and INR depreciation (~10% vs USD) are seen as positives for competitiveness. Management is considering consolidating non-wind order intake to protect focus.
Inputs: pig iron (special grade) and resin imported, ~10-12% of raw material purchases. Commodity prices reportedly rose ~20% after mid-February with a one-quarter pass-through lag.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 revenue guidance ₹500 crore versus the earlier ₹530-550 crore, and what is the margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the order book supports ₹530-550 crore but guided ₹500-530 crore given ramp-up risk from 30-40% new headcount; ₹30 crore above ₹500 crore could add ~100 bps margin.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a margin improvement expected in Q1 FY27 from machining?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no significant Q1 margin contribution expected; Q2 should show margin progress as 50-60% of Q1 time goes to product development.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt position and how is land funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is ~₹165 crore, expected ₹175-180 crore by FY27 end, with debt-to-equity below 1.5; land (~₹25 crore for 15-16 acres) to come from internal accruals, adding only about ₹10 crore to debt.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY28 expansion plan and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Greenfield capex to be decided in Q3 FY27 with ~15 months commissioning; cost to be reassessed (earlier ₹500-600 crore). Equity raise is contemplated around Q4 FY27 to Q2 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Other income is high; what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited FX gains, interest on deposits, and export incentives: duty drawback and RoDTEP at about 2% of export revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sales tonnage and realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 sales ~8,500 MT (not confirmed precisely), production ~6,400 MT; realisation ~₹135-140 per kg-equivalent relation; all exports FOB.

risks_watch: Ramp-up of 45,000 MT foundry and 20,000 MT machining; utilisation target 80% by Q2 and 90%+ by FY28, with product mix complexity (12 new products) and new hires (30-40%) a constraint.

Commodity and energy inflation with a one-quarter pass-through lag; West Asia/Iran-related freight and logistics volatility; FOB exports limit freight exposure but export consignments were reported held up.
Domestic OEM scheduling volatility and seasonality (Q1 slow, Q2 rain-affected); management says 45:55 H1/H2 split.
Power-banking dispute with the state electricity board causing lapsed solar units; policy outcome to monitor.

541929|2026-06.headline: Synergy Green Q1 FY27 revenue of ₹75.71 crore and 7% PBDIT margin were weak; management reiterates ₹500 crore FY27 revenue and 300 bps margin uplift.
541929|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 total income was ₹75.71 crore with absolute PBDIT of ₹5.3 crore at a 7% margin, as dispatches slipped on customer lifting, prototype approval delays and shipping constraints. Production rose about 10% YoY and the new 45,000 tpa capacity reached 66% utilisation in Q1, with July utilisation at 85% (about 3,200 tons). Raw material, consumable and energy inflation (linked to the West Asia conflict and an MSEDCL solar banking change) cut margins, which management expects to partly recover from Q2 via one-quarter-lagged indexation. Management maintained FY27 guidance of ~₹500 crore revenue (33% growth) and ~300 bps PBDIT margin expansion.

segments.name: Wind foundry (SG iron, grey iron, steel castings, 3-30 MT)
segments.commentary: Capacity expanded from 30,000 to 45,000 tpa; FY26 utilisation was 93% on old capacity. Q1 utilisation 66% on new capacity, July at 85%, with 80-90% targeted within 2-3 months.

segments.name: Machining (in-house)
segments.commentary: Machining capacity 20,000 tpa; product development 50% complete and utilisation reached 50% in July. Target 40-50% in-house machining, reducing outsourcing costs.

segments.name: Non-wind (power, mining, L&T, BHEL, Terex)
segments.commentary: BHEL PO received in Q1 (8-9 months development); L&T development underway. Terex order book strong on yen appreciation (~20% vs INR). Non-wind and gearboxes ~30% of revenue.

FY27 full-year PBDIT margin to improve ~300 bps YoY, driven by volumes, export concentration in H2 and machining contribution.

Utilisation target of 80% on full 45,000 tpa capacity for FY27; 80-90% within 2-3 months from July.

Land for 100,000 tpa project targeted by December or March; next project start by Q3 of next year; fundraising ideally Q1/Q2 2028.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity 45,000 tpa (expanded from 30,000 tpa); in-house machining 20,000 tpa; 10 MW captive solar.
Plan for 100,000 tpa capacity; land acquisition targeted by December or March; greenfield capex takes 15-18 months to commission.
Additional 5 MW wind PPA via open access to offset power cost inflation; solar + PPA to cover 50-60% of power needs.
Vestas 4 MW platform: tooling started mid-May; samples expected Q4 FY27, full production Q1 FY28. Nordex NX N 5 MW prototypes cleared in Q1.
Inventory held at 8-10 weeks; target to keep shop order book below 8 weeks.
demand_pricing: Q1 dispatches lower due to delayed customer material lifting and prototype approvals with a key customer; export rollouts hit by ship availability amid West Asia conflict. Unsold production went into inventory.
Furan Resin (third-largest cost item) rose ~60%; PNG/LNG prices up 60-70%; pig iron and CRC inflation from shortages and imported scrap logistics.

Indian suppliers estimated 5-10% cheaper than China on landed cost for wind products after yen appreciation; US market favours non-Chinese suppliers.
Management views wind demand stronger than solar; night-time wind tariffs 25% higher than solar daytime, per management.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 production was strong but did not convert to sales; Q2 execution is at a much higher flow rate, and product approval has come from 50% of customers.

qa_highlights.question: Did realisations spike given 66% utilisation implies ~7,400 MT?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management said produced material was not all sold, creating inventory, and realisation is unchanged, with revenue recognition pending.

qa_highlights.question: Is other income of ₹4.4 crore from power sales?
qa_highlights.answer: No; likely FX-related or export incentives. Management has not sold power; solar lapsed units were lost under the MSEDCL policy change.

qa_highlights.answer: Renamed the executable order book; ₹500 crore set for FY27 given hurdles, with ₹600 crore possible next year on higher capacity.

qa_highlights.question: When will the next capex and fundraising happen?
qa_highlights.answer: Two or three good quarters needed first; land by December or March; project start by Q3 next year; fundraising ideally Q1/Q2 2028.

qa_highlights.answer: Vestas wants more allocation but capacity is going to new OEMs (Nordex, Adani) each allocating ₹100-150 crore; wind is ~₹400 crore of revenue, non-wind and gearboxes ~30%.

qa_highlights.answer: Adani 5 MW parts often exceed 30 MT, so imported from China; Adani 5.2 MW bearing (6-7 ton casting) supplied. Offshore volumes not expected for 5-10 years; company focuses on 3-4 MW onshore.

541967|2026-03.headline: Sky Gold guides FY27 revenue INR8,100 crore and FY30 PAT INR945 crore, targets 50%+ debt reduction in FY27 with working capital cut to 59 days.

Management revised its guidance framing: it will no longer give volume guidance, keeps FY30 PAT of INR945 crore, and sees 30-35% revenue CAGR with an advanced gold model that lowers reported revenue but adds margin. Phase 3 is funded wholly from internal cash, with a net debt-free balance sheet targeted by FY30.

541967|2026-09.headline: Sky Gold Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 61% YoY to INR2,391 crore, with reported PAT of INR129 crore up 93% and H1 operating cash flow positive at INR136 crore.

H1 operating cash flow turned positive at INR136 crore versus an outflow of INR101 crore a year earlier, and net working capital fell to 55 days. Management declined to give forward guidance citing SEBI restrictions and referred to a recent fundraise without disclosing its purpose or size.

rows.label: Insurance distribution regulation from 1 April 2027
rows.why: Management expects a regulatory revenue loss on insurance fees (about 4% of PBT) and targets recovering about 50% via higher attachment rates.

rows.label: Opex-to-assets below 3% medium term
rows.why: Opex-to-assets is 3.33% in H1FY27 and cost-to-income fell to 42.9%; the target of below 40% depends on RO productivity rising from 1.3 toward 1.5 files per month.

542011|2026-03.headline: GRSE posted record FY26: revenue INR 7,002 crore (+38%) and PAT INR 748 crore (+42%), with order book down to INR 15,324 crore.
542011|2026-03.overview: Management reported best-ever Q4 and FY26 results, with Q4 revenue of INR 2,119 crore (+29% YoY) and PAT of INR 303 crore (from INR 244 crore). Eight warships were delivered in FY26, including three on a single day, and the company said revenue from the bridges vertical crossed INR 200 crore for the first time. The order book fell to INR 15,324 crore, the first time it has dropped below INR 20,000 crore in five years, which management attributed to faster execution. The NGC corvette contract (~INR 33,000 crore, GRSE as L1) is still unsigned; management now expects signing in the June quarter, and it pushes NGC revenue recognition to H2 FY28.

financial_highlights.change: vs 8.3% in FY25 (as cited by analyst; includes Q4 provision write-back benefit per analyst)
lower; first time below INR 20,000 crore in five years

segments.name: Warship / defence shipbuilding
segments.commentary: Warship order book about INR 11,361 crore. P-17 Alpha has about INR 5,868 crore remaining, NGOPV INR 5,168 crore and ASW Shallow Water Craft INR 2,035 crore. Eight warships delivered in FY26.

segments.name: Non-defence / commercial vessels
segments.commentary: Order book about INR 3,369 crore across Ocean Research Vessel (INR 749 crore), Coastal Research Vessels (INR 260 crore), Acoustic Research Ship (INR 456 crore), hybrid ferries (INR 207 crore), Multipurpose Vessels (INR 1,345 crore) and dredger (INR 66 crore).

segments.name: Naval guns and portable steel bridges
segments.commentary: Seven naval surface guns delivered in FY26, four completed Sea Acceptance Trials. 110 portable steel bridges delivered, including 30 for export; bridges revenue above INR 200 crore for the first time, export revenue above INR 270 crore.

guidance_outlook: NGC contract (~INR 33,000 crore) expected to be signed in the June 2026 quarter; no revenue planned in FY27 or H1 FY28; revenue to start in H2 FY28, major chunk from FY29.

FY27 revenue accrual expected to be 'very healthy', in line with the last three to four years; FY28 to be padded by remaining projects, NGOPV, commercial vessels and new orders. Management declined to confirm FY28 revenue will not dip.
EBITDA margins expected to be similar in FY27, and management will try to maintain similar margins in FY28 and FY29.
Capacity to rise from 28 platforms to 32 ships by end of calendar 2026 via modernisation; plans for two brownfield and two greenfield yards (West Bengal and Gujarat).

Pipeline of about INR 1,50,000 crore of AoN-accorded RFPs (excluding NGC), with P-17 Bravo (~INR 70,000 crore) RFP expected in the current quarter; MCV (~INR 32,000 crore) and LPD (~INR 35,000 crore) RFPs by end of FY27.
capex_capacity: Current shipbuilding capacity is 28 platforms; expected to rise to 32 ships by end of calendar 2026 through in-premises modernisation.
Planned expansion: two brownfield shipbuilding facilities in West Bengal and two greenfield facilities (one in West Bengal, one in Gujarat).
ASW Shallow Water Craft: four delivered, two at ~80% construction with basin trials done (delivery by mid-calendar 2026), last two at ~60% (delivery in FY27).
P-17 Alpha last ship at ~74% physical progress, delivery targeted in calendar 2026. NGOPV first ship launch planned on 20 May 2026; project completion in FY29.

Ocean Research Vessel ~50% complete, launch planned in calendar 2026. Acoustic Research Ship ~20% complete. 13 hybrid ferries (6 x 200-PAX, 7 x 100-PAX) to finish by end FY27; first two 100-PAX launches planned in May 2026. German 12-ship MPV: keel laid on three ships. Bangladesh dredger launch planned in FY27.
demand_pricing: Next Generation Corvette (NGC): price negotiations complete, ~INR 33,000 crore, GRSE is L1; contract slipped from 31 March 2026 target, now expected in June quarter; management says no red flags. Electronics is 55-60% of equipment cost, with BEL as a major sister-PSU supplier.

Live tenders: Multipurpose Vessels (2 ships, ~INR 1,500 crore, bid submitted), OPV for Coast Guard (5 ships, ~INR 2,000 crore) and 22 Interceptor Boats (~INR 1,000 crore), bids due around end May or early June 2026.

Upcoming RFPs in ~3 months: 120 Fast Interceptor Craft (~INR 3,500 crore, split 80/40), 31 Follow-On Water Jet FACs (~INR 3,500 crore) and seven P-17 Bravo (~INR 70,000 crore, split 4/3). MCV (12 ships, ~INR 32,000 crore, 8/4) and LPD (4 ships, ~INR 35,000 crore, 2/2) RFPs expected by end FY27.

Commercial tenders from Ministry of Shipping: four Platform Support Vessels (INR 1,200-1,500 crore), four MR tankers, six VLGCs and six Aframax vessels. European ship owners are in dialogue, citing pricing and quality versus China and Korea.
Cost escalation: existing contracts are fixed price, and vendor orders were placed earlier, so management reports no material impact; new bids will factor in commodity risk.

qa_highlights.question: Statutory defence committee report shows contracts expected over two years for warships and survey vessels fell to ~INR 18,900 crore from ~INR 42,000 crore. What does this mean for government focus?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said the INR 18,900 crore figure reflects annual fund outflow, not intent. He cited AoNs, RFPs and approved Navy and Coast Guard roadmaps as evidence of continued focus.

qa_highlights.question: Relevance of conventional platforms versus autonomous vessels, and GRSE's strategy in autonomy.
qa_highlights.answer: Conventional platforms remain relevant for armament and endurance. GRSE has developed subsurface and surface autonomous vessels, supplied one to a DRDO organisation, and targets the XL AUV under Make projects in 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the revenue in the 31 March provisional figure materially different from the final reported number?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it had kept a conservative provisional figure because three ships were delivered on the last day. After formalising deliveries and revenue with the Navy, final revenue came to about INR 7,200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is NGC delayed, and when will it be signed? Will there be one or two winners on smaller projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Price negotiations are complete. Contract signing was expected by 31 March but is now expected in the June quarter, with no red flags. Smaller projects are mostly single-yard awards, with 120 FAC and P-17 Bravo split between two yards.

qa_highlights.question: When will NGC revenue start and how will revenue and EBITDA margins look for FY27-FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: NGC revenue recognition starts in H2 FY28, with the major chunk from FY29. Margins are expected to be similar in FY27 and the company will try to maintain them in FY28-FY29. Management did not confirm no FY28 revenue dip.

qa_highlights.question: Are FY25 and FY26 margins inflated by provision write-backs, and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Analyst cited 8.3% EBITDA margin in FY25 and 11.6% in FY26. Management said the current year margins will be similar but would not give a specific percentage, saying it is only Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NGC vendor ecosystem and electronics content?
qa_highlights.answer: Equipment and systems are ~65% of project cost; electronics is 55-60% of that and machinery and systems 40-45%. First downstream orders expected within three months of contract signing, majority within three to six months. BEL expected to be a key partner.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company take large European commercial orders and target higher margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commercial export projects will be selected for good margins. Warship projects, at ~INR 675 crore per ASW ship, still carry the best money and margins. Hybrid large vessels are being targeted.

qa_highlights.question: How are commodity cost increases handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing contracts are fixed price and vendor contracts are fixed price too, so no material impact was reported. Time delays on steel and industrial gas were marginal. New bids will factor in uncertainty.

risks_watch: NGC contract signing has already slipped from 31 March to June quarter; any further delay would push the revenue ramp and reduce FY28 visibility.
Order book of INR 15,324 crore is down sharply; FY28 revenue is not guaranteed without new order wins, and no revenue recognition from NGC is planned until H2 FY28.
Margin sustainability: FY26 margin included provision write-backs per analyst. Management has not quantified the sustainable margin level.

542011|2026-06.headline: GRSE Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 39% YoY to ₹1,815 crore and PAT 44% to ₹173 crore; order book ₹13,596 crore.
542011|2026-06.overview: Management reported total income of ₹1,914 crore (+38% YoY), revenue from operations of ₹1,815 crore (+39%), and PAT of ₹173 crore (+44%) with EPS of ₹15.09 versus ₹10.49. The company said this was its 17th consecutive quarter of upward trend in financials. Order book stands at ₹13,596 crore across 11 projects and 44 marine platforms, and the Next Generation Corvette (NGC) contract is still awaited with management guiding signing within the quarter. Capacity expansion (brownfield and greenfield, roughly ₹4,200 crore combined capex) was the main strategic update, alongside Navratna status granted on 19 June 2026.

financial_highlights.change: First time below ₹15,000 crore in 10 years, per management
Attributed to absence of ship commissioning costs incurred in Q4 FY26
Management called it sinusoidal, tied to delivery phase

Concurrent construction capacity to rise from 28 to 32 platforms by end of calendar 2026; to 43 platforms after Raichak (West Bengal) and western-seaboard facilities.
Management said current quarter's performance can be replicated in coming quarters, citing P-17 Alpha (~₹4,500 crore left) and ASW craft (~₹1,816 crore left) as major execution drivers.
Expects employee cost increase of 15-20% from next pay commission, consistent with past pay commissions.
Bonus or stock split: awaiting directions from administrative ministry and DIPAM.
capex_capacity: P-17 Alpha large ship ~85% complete; delivery targeted by November 2026 (calendar year). First two P-17 Alpha ships delivered ahead of schedule.
Four of eight anti-submarine shallow water craft delivered; remaining four to be delivered in FY27 (fifth ~91%, sixth ~88%, seventh and eighth ~65-70%).
NGOPV: first ship launched, second launched ~11 August 2026; third and fourth launches in Q3 and Q4 FY27; first delivery Q2 FY28, last Q2 FY29.

Expansion capex: ~₹200 crore for two Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port facilities (18-month revitalization, already started); ~₹2,200 crore for Raichak greenfield shipyard in West Bengal (DPR in final stages, 3-5 years to operationalise, infra work from 2027); ~₹2,000 crore for a Gujarat-side total ship solution facility (shipbuilding, green recycling, repair) on PPP model, DPR complete, environmental clearance obtained, ~3 years to operationalise.
demand_pricing: Live defence RFPs ~₹80,000 crore (Navy and Coast Guard): 120 fast interceptor craft ~₹3,500 crore (bid due next month); 31 follow-on water jet FAC ~₹3,500 crore; 22 interceptor boats ~₹1,200-1,300 crore (bids submitted); six NGOPVs for Coast Guard ~₹2,500 crore; P-17 Bravo (DAC AON ₹70,000 crore).
RFPs expected in calendar 2026: mine sounder measure vessel (~₹36,000 crore AON, split between two yards, 8 and 4) and four LPDs (~₹35,000 crore).

Non-defence tenders out via PSU demand aggregation: four MR tankers; six VLGCs and six Aframax vessels (GRSE partnering with a foreign yard and a sister yard); container ship tender expected (partnering with an Indian yard due to lack of dock capacity).
Letters of intent received for four platform support vessels (ONGC) and one green electric tug (SMP Port, Kolkata); GRSE L1 in NGC (~₹ high value, contract awaited).
Water metro opportunity: ₹200-300 crore per metro; ~₹1,500 crore and 30-40 platforms if five states proceed.
Next Generation Destroyer not expected at RFP stage before FY29 per management (no DAC approval yet).
Export strategy: no export orders currently pursued given domestic non-defence demand (~200+ platforms); will consider attractive European orders.
Indigenisation: management says ~80-85% overall by value; weapons ~60%, survival ~70%, float (hull) 100% but ~10% of cost, propulsion engines not yet indigenous; large survey vessel >80%.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the Next Generation Corvette contract been delayed, and when would revenue recognition start if signed today?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the contract slipped from FY26-end/Q1 and is now expected to be signed this quarter, with no red flags seen. Revenue recognition would begin in FY28 after a pre-production design and equipment-ordering phase; the eight-ship project completes around 2034-35.

qa_highlights.question: Does GRSE have capability for unmanned and autonomous naval vessels, and does the expansion plan address it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has capability, citing an unmanned surface vessel prototype, a project for NSTL (DRDO) and an autonomous underwater platform prototype tested about a year ago. It is taking part in Navy-steered autonomy projects and was shortlisted for another underwater unmanned platform.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex quantum for greenfield and brownfield expansion, and what capability will it add?
qa_highlights.answer: Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port revitalisation is about ₹200 crore over 18 months. Raichak greenfield yard in West Bengal is about ₹2,200 crore with 3-5 years to operationalise; the Gujarat-side total ship solution facility is about ₹2,000 crore with about 3 years to operationalise. Capacity goes from 32 to 43 platforms, including larger Aframax/VLGC-type vessels.

qa_highlights.question: How will GRSE participate in large commercial tenders (MR tankers, VLGC, Aframax, container ships) given capacity limits?
qa_highlights.answer: MR tankers and VLGCs are being bid with a sister yard and, for VLGC, a foreign yard with proven capability. Container ships are being pursued through a partnership with an Indian yard that has the dock and berth infrastructure, as GRSE lacks physical capacity for them.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 execution momentum be sustained, or will growth slow from the ~35-40% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current quarter's performance can be replicated, pointing to about ₹4,500 crore left on P-17 Alpha and about ₹1,816 crore on anti-submarine craft. It noted FY26 delivered eight ships and that the next quarter should see deliveries and higher contract workforce costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the indigenisation level and where is GRSE still import-dependent?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall indigenisation is about 80-85% by value. Hull/float is 100% but about 10% of cost, weapons about 60%, survival about 70%, and diesel alternators 100%; propulsion engines are not yet indigenous. Bailey Bridge is 100%, deck machinery about 90%, and the diesel engine co-production targets 55-60%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp fall in other expenses and employee costs QoQ, and what is the pay commission impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses fell because Q4 FY26 included commissioning costs for three ships that did not recur. Contract workforce cost is sinusoidal with delivery timing and will rise when a couple of ships deliver. Management expects the next pay commission to add 15-20% to employee costs, in line with past commissions.

542066|2026-03.headline: Adani Total Gas Q4 FY26 revenue rose 16% to INR1,696 crore and EBITDA 13% to INR310 crore; management guided FY27 EBITDA to about INR1,500 crore.
542066|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 16% YoY to INR1,696 crore and EBITDA rose 13% to INR310 crore, with PAT up 4% to INR156 crore. For FY26, revenue grew 18% to INR6,415 crore, EBITDA rose 5% to INR1,225 crore, PBT fell 1% to INR863 crore and PAT was INR637 crore. Volumes carried the quarter: CNG grew 17% YoY in Q4 and PNG 5%, with a record ~50,000 domestic PNG connections added. Management said the West Asia crisis raised gas costs, which were partly absorbed to protect consumers, and that gas pool supply from the government was used to keep CNG and domestic PNG supplied.

segments.name: PNG (domestic)
segments.commentary: PNG volumes grew 5% YoY in Q4 and 6% in FY26. Total household tally reached 1.1 million (ATGL standalone) and 13.1 lakh including the IOAGPL JV.

segments.name: Industrial and commercial
segments.commentary: 214 customers added in Q4, taking the total to 9,965. Management said industrial volumes saw about 1% degrowth here and there during the crisis; industrial is about 20% and commercial about 2.5% of volume.

segments.name: E-mobility (ATEL)
segments.commentary: Operates 5,100 EV charge points across 26 states and UTs and 226 cities, with about 54 MW installed capacity. Target of 10,000 charge points in the near term.

FY27 EBITDA growth to track volume growth; management cited around INR1,500 crore of EBITDA for FY27.
Government targets natural gas at 15% of the energy mix by 2030; ATGL positions itself to support this.

demand_pricing: Gas pool price for March 2026 was USD 12.42 per MMBtu; the pool mixed domestic gas, withdrawn RLNG and fertiliser volumes, ONGC consumption, Vedanta and HPHT gas, and later contracted LNG.

Q4 CNG (T) gas sourcing: about 85% from APM allocation plus HPHT and WG volumes and other contracts; about 16% bought spot. Portfolio also includes Brent-linked and asset-linked contracts.

Management said price was calibrated and not fully passed through to consumers to protect volumes, citing consumer-first approach.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gas pool price formula and which gases are in it (Dolat Capital)?
qa_highlights.answer: Pool price is the weighted average of pooled volumes: RLNG, fertiliser and ONGC volumes withdrawn, plus Vedanta and HPHT gas. March 2026 pool price was USD 12.42 per MMBtu; imported LNG was excluded in March but included later in April.

542066|2026-09.headline: Adani Total Gas Q2 FY27 volumes rose 12% YoY to 315 MMSCM and EBITDA 12% to INR340 crore, while PAT grew only 3% to INR167 crore amid a 43% gas cost surge.

542650|2026-03.headline: Metropolis Q4 FY26 organic revenue grew 14.7% to INR 392 crores, with organic EBITDA margin at 27.2%, up from 18.5%.
542650|2026-03.overview: Organic revenue grew 14.7% YoY in Q4 FY26 to INR 392 crores, driven by 9.3% patient volume growth and about 5% realisation improvement, with no price increase taken in the quarter due to GST reasons. Organic EBITDA margin rose to 27.2% (from 18.5%) and full-year organic margin reached 25.9%, up about 140 bps after adjusting for prior-year acquisition costs. Management said the heavy lab and centre build-out is largely done, so the focus shifts to throughput-led productivity, and it guided to 14% to 15% revenue CAGR and a 27% to 28% group EBITDA margin over three years. Core Diagnostics reached a high-single-digit margin in Q4, meeting the 4-quarter turnaround commitment.

qa_highlights.question: Will you take a price hike this fiscal, and what margin improvement is achievable next year?

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 14% to 15% growth comes from volume versus realisation?

542650|2026-06.headline: Metropolis Q1 FY27 revenue rose 17% YoY to INR 450 crore with EBITDA margin up 210 bps to 25.2%, driven mostly by volume.
542650|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew about 17% YoY to INR 450 crore, ahead of guidance, with 10% patient volume and 11% test volume growth and no price increase in 18 months. EBITDA rose 27% YoY to INR 113 crore (25.2% margin, +210 bps) and PAT rose 26% to INR 57 crore (12.6% margin, +90 bps). Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth of 14-15% and a 100-150 bps EBITDA margin improvement, with a 27-28% margin target over the next two years. Network expansion continued (300 centers added in Q1, 500+ planned), while the company pruned about 300 low-productivity centers.

qa_highlights.answer: B2C patient volume grew about 13.5% and B2B about 6%. Management attributed Q1 strength to market-access execution and seasonal momentum, but could not fully dissect it; possible overflow from Q4 was one theory.

qa_highlights.question: Does Metropolis run O&M or regional lab management with standalone labs, with profit-share arrangements?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it already runs a lab-on-lease model for about 10 years, taking over pathologist-run labs fully. Number of such labs was not given; to be followed up.

qa_highlights.question: Is the TruHealth Mind and Body initiative a blend of genomics and advanced radiology, and what growth is targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: TruHealth combines blood tests with vitals, basic radiology (X-ray, ECG, sonography) and cognitive/mental health checks. Genomics is not part of it yet. No package-level targets were set.

qa_highlights.answer: CGHS is about 1% of revenue, so the one-time price revision benefit is small. Management expects CGHS empanelment to keep growing, though the one-time benefit will not recur next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the guidance of 14-15% growth conservative, and is Q1 a one-off versus the base-rate growth of peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 14-15% for the year, citing a track record of delivering that range over the last two quarters. It declined to focus on quarter-by-quarter seasonality, noting weather-driven unpredictability.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not expand beyond 750 towns and has halted lab expansion for about five quarters, so new towns and labs should not add margin stress. It relies on operating leverage and productivity gains. Tier-2/3 economics were said to be no worse than metros.

542651|2026-03.headline: KPIT Q4 FY26 revenue grew 1.8% in constant currency and 12% YoY in rupees; management guides FY27 EBITDA margin of 20.5-21.2% as two large SDV programs ramp down.
542651|2026-03.overview: KPIT closed Q4 FY26 with 1.8% constant-currency and 1.9% QoQ dollar growth, 12% YoY and 5.8% QoQ in rupees, and EBITDA margin of 20.6% for the quarter and 20.8% for the year. Management booked $349 million of TCV in the quarter, with 21% of pipeline in products and solutions. The call flagged the planned ramp-down of two large SDV programs (one with a European OEM, one a surprise stop by a Japanese OEM after Honda cancelled new platforms in April), which will weigh on Q1 FY27 revenue by an estimated 3-4% QoQ. Management guided FY27 EBITDA to 20.5-21.2% and a medium-term 22-24% margin, with solutions and products growing 30% a year.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is 3-4% of quarterly revenue, starting Q1 FY27, and it expects to cover it with pipeline in existing clients and new accounts.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the move to a 22-24% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Products and solutions carry higher gross margins, reusable assets and AI-infused work improve margins, fixed-price conversion helps, and AI lowers SG&A.

qa_highlights.question: How does KPIT compete with Chinese automotive engineering firms that run lower margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishor said KPIT competes favourably outside China and already sells products to top China OEMs; Sachin said China's advantage is EV platforms and batteries, which are complementary.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 TCV jump, and is that repeatable?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishor said the jump came from off-highway commercial wins and traditional clients; Sachin said quarterly variability is normal but half-yearly and yearly TCV is growing.

542651|2026-06.headline: KPIT Q1 FY27: constant-currency revenue grew only 0.1% YoY and fell 3.6% QoQ, with EBITDA margin at 17.2% and PAT at INR 1.17 billion.
542651|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was roughly flat YoY in constant currency (+0.1%) and down 0.6% YoY in USD, with QoQ constant-currency revenue down 3.6%, against management's earlier guide of about 1% YoY degrowth and about 5% QoQ decline. Profitability fell more than proportionally: EBITDA margin was 17.2%, EBIT margin 12.3%, and PAT INR 1.17 billion, hit by forex losses and a share of losses from Qorix tied to postponed European revenues. Deal wins were USD 257 million, led by connected cars, aftersales transformation and autonomous. Management guided H2 better than H1, with a return to growth by Q4, and said margin recovery will largely follow revenue recovery.

qa_highlights.answer: Kishor Patil said the weakness is not permanent; CV was hit by a one-time large license deal in the prior quarter and growth is expected next quarter. He said the uncertainty is about when deals will realise, not whether KPIT gets its share.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 22% to 24% margin aspiration for FY29 from the Analyst Day still hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishor Patil said the medium-term outlook remains good, with product and solutions revenue expected to grow and be margin accretive, and some solutions ready to deploy in the next quarter or two; outcome-based models are also part of the plan.

542651|2026-09.headline: KPIT Q2 FY27 revenue rose 6.5% YoY in rupee terms (0.2% YoY in CC) as off-highway and CV grew 27% YoY, offsetting a 13%+ revenue drop from two top OEMs.
542651|2026-09.overview: Management said Q2 was in line with its own expectations, with growth of 6.5% YoY and 1% QoQ in rupee terms, and 0.5% QoQ and 0.2% YoY in constant currency. Passenger car revenue fell about 8% YoY and 4% QoQ, driven by sharp declines at two top accounts (one in Japan, one in Europe) that together were 13% of total revenue. Off-highway and commercial vehicles grew 27% YoY and 17.6% QoQ, and Products revenue grew 5% QoQ and 25% YoY. EBITDA margin rose 60 bps to 17.8% on mix, while net cash fell to about INR 6.2 billion on dividends, the Cymotive payment and a DSO increase from 51 to 53 days.

segments.name: Passenger car
segments.commentary: Down about 8% YoY and 4% QoQ; excluding the two top accounts (13% of revenue) the decline was absorbed by off-highway, CV and Products growth. Management expects the two accounts to bottom out over the next couple of quarters.

segments.name: Off-highway and commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Grew 27% YoY and 17.6% QoQ. Off-highway has 3 clients with 2 more being added; SDM consulting engagements rose to 3 (one program launch expected next year per Korea comment).

segments.name: Products
segments.commentary: Grew 5% QoQ and 25% YoY; management will share product revenue more fully next year, with detailed reporting possibly early next year.

segments.name: Geographies
segments.commentary: Europe and Japan declined on the two OEM exits; Americas grew QoQ and YoY; SIMA (now split from Asia) grew, led by India. Vietnam investment being doubled for a Chinese Tier 1 centre and an existing OEM.

The two top OEM accounts expected to bottom out in the next couple of quarters, with gradual recovery into early next year.
European OEM consolidation expected to be meaningfully concluded by end of Q1 FY28; impact in H1 next year.
EBITDA expected to rise every quarter, with return toward the earlier 20-21% range only early next year.
QORIX programs pushed out: Gen 4 programs moved from 2028 to 2029-30; no stabilisation timeline given.
capex_capacity: R&D spend increased by a couple of million dollars QoQ in the quarter.
Vietnam subsidiary being scaled up, including a centre with a large Chinese Tier 1 to deliver China OEM global programs outside China.
Cost mix may shift from high-cost to low-cost centres as clients move to remote delivery; technology investment teams will not be optimised.
Energytech and deep-tech adjacency offerings being built; early wins expected in 2-3 quarters, meaningful impact takes longer.
demand_pricing: Wins were mainly in Autonomy, Connected and IDART; 89% of wins came from target accounts.
Passenger car weakness at two OEMs (Japan and Europe) with cancelled programs or cut spend; European passenger car OEMs cutting costs and sourcing from India.
Trucks in North America showing signs of growth; off-highway expected to keep growing; European PASSCAR OEMs still struggling.
AI platform: over 9,000 users, 5 million+ transactions and 12,000 engineering agents built in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Are the two large customer declines bottoming, and can Asia and Europe recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Tikekar said both OEMs (one in Japan under JKC, one in Europe) should bottom out in the next couple of quarters, with gradual growth returning early next year; Americas grew and India drove SIMA growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the cash flow decline in H1 due to working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Priya Hardikar cited dividend, Cymotive acquisition payment and higher DSO, which lifted the working capital cycle; she did not quantify the cash conversion.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to 20-21% EBITDA as growth accelerates?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishor Patil said margins will rise somewhat every quarter, with a return toward earlier levels only early next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the CV segment's growth broad-based and sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said off-highway is concentrated on 3 clients but broadening with 2 more being added, and trucks should pick up in coming quarters on North America recovery.

qa_highlights.question: What is the QORIX outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishor Patil said programs were pushed out by a couple of years; Anup Sable said Gen 4 programs moved from 2028 to 2029-30, and management is exploring adjacencies such as robotics and more partners.

qa_highlights.question: Will employee costs rise in line with revenue given fixed-price growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishor Patil said AI leverage and products/solutions growth will drive operating leverage, but not across all clients; headcount additions depend on client adaptability.

risks_watch: Continued weakness at the two top OEMs (about 13% of revenue) beyond the expected two-quarter bottoming.
Attrition rose to mid-teens in Q2; management expects it to fall substantially next quarter after increments.

QORIX losses and delayed Gen 4 programs with no stabilisation timeline.
