542652|2026-03.headline: Polycab Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 27% YoY with EBITDA margin at 13.1% and record quarterly PAT of INR 7.9 bn, while Cable & Wire volumes grew only low single digits.
542652|2026-03.overview: Management reported record annual and quarterly revenue, with Q4 consolidated revenue up 27% YoY and PAT of INR 7.9 bn (up 7%, 8.9% margin). Growth was price-led: cumulative price hikes of 18-19% were taken from January to March, while Cable & Wire volumes grew low single digits in the quarter. Middle East escalation, PVC price spikes and pollution-related construction halts hit March, which is the key month of Q4. FY26 was a record year: revenue above INR 285 bn (+29%), EBITDA margin 13.9%, PAT above INR 27 bn (+32%), and FY26 volume growth of 18%.

segments.name: Wires & Cables
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 30% YoY, with domestic cables up 30% and combined volume growth in low single digits. EBIT margin was 13.1%, and Q4 EBITDA margin was around 14%+. Cables outpaced wires, and institutional sales grew faster than channel.

segments.name: FMEG
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 47% YoY, the ninth straight quarter of outperformance versus industry. EBIT margin was 4.1%, and FY26 EBITDA margin was mid-single digit. Solar was the largest FMEG category, growing 2x; premium fans were about 25% and premium lighting about 35% of segment revenue.

segments.name: International (exports)
segments.commentary: Grew 18% YoY and contributed 4.4% of consolidated revenue in Q4. Full-year export share was 5.4%, and Middle East was about 16% of FY26 exports, which was hit during the quarter.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue fell 15% YoY to INR 5,098 mn on project execution timing. Segment profit was INR 386 mn, a 7.6% margin. Sustainable margin is guided at mid to high single digits.

guidance_outlook: Project Spring: Cables & Wires to grow at 1.5x industry growth; FMEG at 1.5x-2x industry growth.
Near to mid-term EBITDA margin guided at 12-14%; long-term 11-13%.
Exports to reach more than 10% of revenue by FY30; management expects exports to grow beyond 5% in FY27 and hopes to get there sooner.
Working capital cycle expected to revert to 45-50 days from 25 days in Q4.
Dividend payout to exceed 30% by FY30 (27.2% in FY26).
Capex of INR 60-80 bn over 5 years; FY27 capex guided at INR 12-16 bn per year; FY30 capex of INR 60-80 bn cited as Project Spring target.
EHV capacity expected on stream by end of calendar 2026, with revenue contribution from FY28.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation is mid-70s (75-76%); management says plants practically reach early 90s but a sustainable level is 80-85%.
FY26 capex was about INR 14.8 bn, including roughly INR 15 bn invested in capacity expansion; the company plans INR 1.2-1.6 bn of capacity addition every year.
Around 90% of capex goes to Cable & Wire capacity (largely fungible), about 5% to backward integration and 3-4% to FMEG.
EHV (extra high voltage) capacity is on track to be commissioned by end of calendar 2026; about 50% of domestic EHV consumption is imported.
Management says there will be no scenario where Polycab runs out of capacity over the next 4-5 years.
demand_pricing: Cumulative price hikes of about 18-19% were taken from January to March; pass-through of copper, aluminium and PVC is described as complete and in tandem with input costs.
Volume growth was low single digits in Q4 as West Asia tensions, pollution-related construction halts and PVC price spikes (60-80% in early March) hit primary and secondary sales.
FY26 Cable & Wire volume growth was 18%, versus industry growth of 11-12%, with domestic wires and cable organised market share at 30-31% (up 300-400 bps over FY25's 26-27%).
Channel is about 90% of business and institutional about 10%; channel margins are 3-4% higher than institutional. Institutional mix was 2-3 points higher in Q4.
Demand sectors: power 40-45% of cables, manufacturing and private industry 35-40%, mobility 10-12%, energy and exploration 5-6%.
Power capacity additions in FY26 were about 55-56 GW, nearly double FY25; management expects demand to defer by weeks, not be lost.

qa_highlights.question: What were the Cable & Wire volume growth and price hikes taken from January?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined volume growth was low single digits, with cables ahead of wires. Cumulative price hikes were about 18-19% from January to March.

qa_highlights.question: What was the impact of the Middle East disruption in March?
qa_highlights.answer: Primary sales were hit as distributors lifted less, since secondary sales did not move at the expected pace. Private sector demand was hit by gas rationing, and PVC prices rose 60-80% in early March. The impact was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Institutional mix and margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Institutional sales were about 2-3 points higher than channel in Q4 (about 13-14% of the Cable & Wire top line in Q4 per management's arithmetic). Channel margins are 3-4% higher.

qa_highlights.question: Peak utilisation and capacity headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 75-76%. Management says early 90s has been reached at times, but 80-85% is the sustainable level, and there is room for growth.

qa_highlights.question: Use of surplus cash and M&A?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus remains on capex funded from internal accruals and on the dividend payout. M&A is being evaluated in India and abroad, but nothing is in view for the near to mid term.

qa_highlights.question: Export outlook for FY27 and the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a firm number, but expects exports to exceed the current 5.4% share. US distribution was re-established and North America was about 40% of FY26 exports. Middle East was about 15-16% of FY26 exports and is not expected to contribute meaningfully in the near term.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory gains and raw material hedging?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says there are no inventory gains or losses because raw materials are hedged for copper and aluminium, and copper is largely imported. XLPE and compound availability is comfortable for about one quarter, with a diversified vendor base.

qa_highlights.question: Segment EBITDA margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Cable & Wire Q4 EBITDA margin was around 14%+, and above the 13.9% company level for FY26. FMEG was mid-single digit for both Q4 and FY26.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict, Brent around USD 100/bbl and a record-low rupee (INR 94.83/USD) raise input and inflation risk; the company's stated pass-through has so far held.
Working capital at 25 days in Q4 is flattered by letter-of-credit payables; reversion to 45-50 days would absorb cash.
Institutional mix rising reduces margins (channel is 3-4% higher); watch the mix next quarter.
March volume shortfall: whether primary sales recover as secondary sales normalise, and whether stocking unwinds.
FMEG margins (EBIT 4.1%) remain well below the 8-10% EBITDA target for FY30; watch the trajectory.
Export share fell to 4.4% in Q4; Middle East recovery timing and the US distribution ramp are open questions.
EHV commissioning by end of calendar 2026 and first revenue in FY28.

542652|2026-06.headline: Polycab Q1 FY27: consolidated revenue up 39% YoY, record PAT of INR 7,967 million (+33% YoY), EBITDA margin 13.8%.

542652|2026-09.headline: Polycab Q2 FY27 revenue rose 53% YoY with PAT of INR 9,900 million (+43%) and EBITDA margin of 14.4%, all record highs.

542665|2026-03.headline: Neogen Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 247 crore with 17.8% EBITDA margin; FY27 standalone guidance INR 875-950 crore.
542665|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 22% YoY to INR 247 crore, almost entirely volume-driven, with EBITDA up 21% to INR 44 crore and margin at 17.8% despite Dahej replacement and toll manufacturing costs. PAT was INR 11 crore for the quarter and INR 29 crore for FY26 on revenue of INR 862 crore. Battery materials (Neogen Ionics) remain the core growth push: Dahej Phase 1 is budgeted at INR 428 crore and Pakhajan Phase 2 revised to INR 1,367 crore, with commissioning now guided within FY27. Management kept FY27 standalone revenue guidance at INR 875-950 crore, excluding battery sales, and separately guided INR 300 crore-plus from battery chemicals, weighted to H2.

Battery chemicals revenue guided at INR 300 crore-plus for FY27, mostly in H2 with sequential growth each quarter; excludes commodity price upside.

Electrolyte commercial manufacturing targeted for H1 FY27; electrolyte salt in H2 FY27. Dahej Phase 1 (1,000 tons balance plus 500 tons intermediate) targeted by Q3 FY27, with SCOD of February 2027 approved by lenders; Pakhajan Phase 2 SCOD March 2027.

FY28 tentative target of around INR 1,100 crore plus at full utilisation for the standalone business; FY28 battery revenue expected INR 1,200-1,400 crore by management estimate; FY29 consolidated revenue of INR 3,700-4,200 crore cited (standalone INR 1,200-1,250 crore plus battery INR 2,500-2,900 crore).

Pakhajan electrolyte plant completed mechanical assembly and entered trial run; 30,000 tonne electrolyte plant under trial production, built on Mitsubishi technology per management.
Salt and additive capacity at Dahej: 5,500 tonnes total (about 4,000 tonnes salt and 750-1,500 tonnes additive), plus 500 tonnes intermediate over and above.

Remaining FY27 capex around INR 600-700 crore for Neogen Ionics plus about INR 100 crore for Neogen; no major capex planned for FY28 at present. Neogen Ionics gross block expected INR 1,700-1,800 crore at end-FY27; standalone gross block INR 450-550 crore.
Organolithium capacity raised 2.5x to 300 tonnes per year from about 120 tonnes; management expects 80-90% utilisation this year and a small capex possible next year.
demand_pricing: Lithium carbonate around USD 24-25/kg versus management's long-term stable band of USD 15-25 (centre about USD 20); management does not factor commodity upside into guidance because it is passed through.
Bromine prices elevated but stable after shipments from Dead Sea Bromine; contracts limited the Q4 impact. Management budgets bromine at about INR 300 plus or minus 50.

Chinese LiPF6 salt pricing was 30-50% below Neogen's formula price at start of the year; the gap is now about 20-25%. Electrolyte pricing guided at USD 6-8/kg (current lithium price about USD 7-9/kg), with USD 7-7.5 as average.

Two electrolyte customers have qualified Neogen; two more are validating Neogen electrolyte against Chinese electrolyte; two more start in 2027. Management says US electrolyte makers' site audits are complete with commercial clearances pending.
The domestic giga-factory customer is expanding from 1 GWh to 5 GWh in H1 2026 and is currently sourced solely from Neogen.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROCE should remain at 18-20% after revision, citing raw material savings, and that the added 500 MT intermediate capacity is a further source of revenue.

qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to longer supplier credit terms negotiated during the fire, some supplier factoring, and expects debtors and creditors to converge over 2-3 years as insurance money arrives.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said peak debt will remain as earlier at about INR 1,700 crore because INR 160 crore promoter equity and USD 20 million JV equity cover the increase.

qa_highlights.question: Is the lower Q4 inventory a sign of a problem, and what drove the rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory rose because of rented outside capacity winding down in March 2026 and Dahej not being online, so stock was built for Q1-Q2 sales.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank moratorium cover interest and principal?
qa_highlights.answer: Moratorium is for principal only, running one year from the revised commercial operation start date; interest is charged from COD and interest during construction is included in project cost.

qa_highlights.answer: Most Dahej capacity is Neogen's own technology, with Morita adjustments made mainly at Pakhajan; the additive salt line has no Morita tie-up.

Net profit fell to Rs 50 crore in Q4 because of a Rs 34 crore mark-to-market loss on treasury bonds, versus Rs 475 crore for the full year. Paying suppliers rose 3,200 in FY26 to 2.2 lakh but declined 1,200 in Q4, which management attributes to a Silver tier price increase at the end of Q2 and the war that broke out in late February. Management gave no net-add guidance and said it is not reversing pricing.

542759|2026-03.headline: Spandana returned to profit in Q4 FY26 with PAT of INR5 crore, ending six loss-making quarters, as AUM grew 12% QoQ to INR4,420 crore.
542759|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 marked the first quarterly profit after six quarters, with PAT of INR5 crore versus a loss of INR95 crore in Q3 and PBT of INR8 crore versus a loss of INR125 crore. AUM rose 12% QoQ to INR4,420 crore, the first AUM increase after eight quarters, with disbursements up to about INR500 crore per month from INR400 crore in Q3. Opex fell to about INR161 crore from INR195 crore, and PPOP rose to INR39 crore from INR8 crore. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 3.8% (4.2% in Dec-25), NNPA at 0.73% and X-bucket collection efficiency at 99.7%. NIM contracted to 9.9% from 11.1% as borrowing costs stayed high.

Customer base is a little over 11.5 lakh, with 1.2 lakh new borrowers added in Q4 versus about 63,000 in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 1 April 2026 mutual fund yield cut hit B&K transaction revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is about 2-3% on a base of about Rs 200-225 crore a quarter, which is not material, and is offset by synergies.

qa_highlights.question: Industry consolidation, competition, and attrition in UHNI?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes the industry needs 3-4 or more large players but remains fairly consolidated for the next 3-4 years. It expects 2-4% attrition a year and sees 12-15% flows as doable.

qa_highlights.question: Quality of new clients, carry exits, and gross flows?

B&K/360 ONE Capital: the MF yield cut from 1 April 2026 (about 2-3% impact on Rs 200-225 crore quarterly base), TBR sustainability, and banking hiring (12 professionals, about 4 in place) with IB contribution expected in 12-18 months.

Management said the 10-12% traditional catering margin range is the target.

Management said it will push for a higher convenience fee but cannot force a policy decision.

542857|2026-09.headline: Greenpanel Q2 FY27 revenue rose 4.6% YoY to INR407 crore, but consolidated operating EBITDA margin fell to 7.5% from 9.6% in Q1 on price cuts.
542857|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR407 crore, up 4.6% YoY and 16.4% QoQ, while total volume declined 3.4% YoY as OEM and export volumes lagged despite record retail MDF sales. Management cut prices to regain share after a steep Q1 price increase, which compressed ASPs by 6-7% QoQ and pushed consolidated operating EBITDA margin to 7.5%. Opening inventory carried from Q1 kept the benefit of the ~5% QoQ fall in cost of production out of Q2 results. Management guided to mid-teen MDF volume growth for FY27 and said H2 pickup is visible, though margin recovery depends on volume and chemical costs.

segments.name: Retail MDF and plywood
segments.commentary: Retail MDF sales in Q2 FY27 were the highest ever for the company in a single quarter, up 17% YoY; plywood sales rose 8.4% YoY. Management says retail earns more than OEM or export, with a margin differential of 5% to 20%.

segments.name: OEM (domestic converters)
segments.commentary: OEM was about 15% of domestic volume in H1 FY27, versus 25-30% a year earlier. Volume fell after the Q1 price increase removed OEM pricing benefits, and OEMs shifted to imports; management expects a return toward 20-25% share over time.

segments.name: Export MDF
segments.commentary: About 85% of exports go to the Middle East. Opening October export order book was about 13,000 cubic meters, but execution was constrained by container availability. Basic 18mm interior-grade export prices were about USD 200-220 per cubic meter FOB.

guidance_outlook: Targets mid-teen MDF volume growth for FY27 full year, with retail growing strongly and the H1 shortfall in OEM and export recovered in H2.
Aims for volume growth in line with the industry (15% and above) from Q3 or Q4 FY27; management said 'hope' rather than firm commitment.

Targets net asset turn of 1.3x to 1.5x at capacity on a sustainable basis; no new capex currently in line.
capex_capacity: Current capacity is about 2,800-2,900 cubic meters per day, roughly 900,000 cubic meters per annum; Line 3 at Andhra Pradesh is already in operation, providing organic headroom.
No capex currently in line for the next few years, per the analyst's question and management's acknowledgement.
Industry capacity additions of about 800,000-900,000 cubic meters per year expected over the next 2 years.

Management indicated a new 250,000 cubic meter MDF plant costs about INR800-850 crore (per a peer's reported figure); a single larger line costs about 25-30% more than one half its size.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 price increase was about 15%, lifting domestic ASP 13.5% QoQ; Q2 saw price realignment and ASPs fell 6-7% QoQ as the company chose to be price-aggressive.
Export demand is intact: opening October export order book exceeded total Q2 export sales, but containers and vessel availability limited execution amid Middle East disruption and sea freight hikes.
Imports are no longer cheaper than domestic supply after freight and chemical cost increases.

Management expects oversupply for at least the next 2 years, with pricing pressure but a narrowing supply-demand gap; multi-daylight press capacity is becoming unviable and some smaller players are exiting or stopping production.
Competition in South India is rising with new plants from Action (first Gujarat plant commissioned in October 2026) and Rushil Decor; management says Action typically does not undercut.

qa_highlights.question: Why has OEM volume not recovered and will it improve in the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Q1 price increase removed OEM pricing benefits, and OEMs placed longer-term import orders that lingered into Q2. It hopes Q3 OEM volumes will be much better than Q2, with October moving in the right direction but not yet at expected levels.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 5% cost-of-production reduction reflect in margins in Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said chemical prices are volatile and hard to predict. It said the Q2 margin hit came from opening inventory of about 50,000 cubic meters made at higher cost; higher utilisation would add operating leverage, and fixed cost per cubic meter has fallen.

qa_highlights.question: Why are realisations lower than smaller peers such as Greenply and Century?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its large OEM and interior mix lowers the value-added share of its average realisation. It claimed that on like-for-like products it is at par with Action, at a premium to Greenply and Century.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 OEM share and the expected H2 and FY28 share?
qa_highlights.answer: OEM was about 15% of domestic volume in H1 FY27, versus 25-30% last year. Management expects a return to 20-25% as retail grows.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export order value and H2 export expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave an opening October export order book of about 13,000 cubic meters, valued at about USD 200-220 per cubic meter FOB for basic 18mm interior grade. Container availability was the main constraint on execution.

qa_highlights.question: What are the EBITDA margins by business, and is double-digit MDF margin achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said retail makes more money, with a 5-20% margin differential, and gave no separate export EBITDA per cubic meter. Management said double-digit MDF margin is its aim and hope.

542867|2026-03.headline: CSB Bank FY26 net profit rose 7% to Rs.633 crore; Q4 profit Rs.202 crore (+32% QoQ) with GNPA at a low 1.66%.
542867|2026-03.overview: CSB Bank closed FY26 with net profit of Rs.633 crore (+7% YoY) and Q4 net profit of Rs.202 crore, up 32% QoQ, with Q4 RoA of 1.53% and RoE of 17.66%. Advances grew 27% and deposits 20% YoY, both ahead of industry, but deposit growth leaned on bulk/wholesale deposits (around 50% of term deposits) and gold loans rose to about 53% of the book. Asset quality improved to GNPA 1.66% and NNPA 0.40%, helped by lower slippages and higher recoveries. Management guided retail asset growth only from FY28, CTI of 60-65% through FY27, and RoA/RoE of about 1.5%/15% next year.

rows.why: 862 branches and 832 ATMs, with transaction banking systems (Vayana, Aurion Pro CMS, trade) going live in 3-4 months and the Dubai representative office approved but delayed; these are systems and offices, not sizeable physical capacity.

542867|2026-06.headline: CSB Bank Q1 FY27 net profit rose 27% YoY to Rs.150 Crores, with NIM at 3.66% and ROA at 1.09%, but other income fell 7%.
542867|2026-06.overview: CSB Bank reported Q1 FY27 net profit of Rs.150 Crores (+27% YoY) and operating profit of Rs.251 Crores (+14% YoY), with NII up 26% to Rs.479 Crores. Deposits grew 26% and advances 24% YoY, both ahead of industry, and CD ratio moved to just under 90%. Other income fell 7% YoY on lower treasury gains (Rs.12 Crores vs Rs.53 Crores) and weaker insurance and gold-linked processing fees. Management called Q1 the worst-case margin quarter and reiterated FY27 NIM of around 3.75% and ROA of 1.3%-1.5%.

financial_highlights.value: Rs.12 Crores treasury profit plus Rs.3 Crores trading profit (total other income down 7%)
Growth 24% YoY vs industry 18.6%; yield on advances 10.65%

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: About 54% of the loan book; yield 11.85% vs 12% QoQ. Management expects the gold mix to stay near 50% in FY27 and fall toward 30% by FY2030. Gold disbursements fell QoQ on regulatory implementation and reduced top-ups; the book was about Rs.21,000 Crores last quarter.

segments.name: Wholesale (WSB)
segments.commentary: About 26% of the book; growing 35%-40% per management. Target is about 32% of the book by FY2030. FIPS book fell to about one-third of WSB from about 70%.

segments.name: SME / BLG
segments.commentary: Yield fell to 9.25% from 9.81% QoQ. Slippages in the quarter; management is deliberately cautious and has raised credit appraisal bars for FY27.

segments.name: Retail (LAS / repledger)
segments.commentary: Repledger LAS book fell from over Rs.2,100 Crores to about Rs.60 Crores and will run off by next quarter, per RBI discontinuation from 1 April 2026. Unsecured retail is only about 2% of the book; focus deferred to FY2028.

segments.name: Treasury and fee income
segments.commentary: Treasury profit was Rs.12 Crores vs Rs.53 Crores a year ago, and insurance fees fell after tighter mis-selling controls. Management targets full-year fee income at 16%-17% of total income, with Q1 other income about 15% of income.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 NIM guidance of around 3.75%; management said it sees no risk to this guidance.
Full-year FY27 ROA guidance of 1.3%-1.5%; management said it would not go below 1.3% this year and internal target is 1.5%.
ROE: started FY27 near 12%; aims to end FY27 above the FY26 exit of 14.14% and try to touch 15%.
Wholesale to grow 35%-40% and gold 30%-35% in FY27; gold mix expected near 50% this year.
CASA to grow in line with deposits from FY2028; CASA to outgrow term deposits from FY2029. FY27 CASA ratio expected to hold at about 19.4% only if deposits grow about 25%.
Fee income guidance of 16%-17% of total income for the full year, with insurance and gold disbursements expected to pick up from Q2.
Unsecured retail push deferred to FY2028; ECLGS disbursement so far about Rs.60 Crores.
capex_capacity: Network of 868 branches and 835 ATMs as on 30 June 2026.
Technology transformation complete: 50+ surrounding systems integrated with CBS, plus transaction banking and ServiceNow; some trade, supply chain and CMS systems to go live in the next 3-4 months.
New retail liability acquisition channel rolling out; retail deposit products launched last year, with sales team being built.
Technology was delayed by about two and a half years, per management, due to a decision delay rather than execution.
demand_pricing: Deposit growth 26% YoY vs industry 13.4%; bulk deposits about 52% of term deposits and about 40% of total deposits; retail about 48% of deposits.
Cost of funds around 6.5%; higher cost driven by bulk deposits, FCY borrowings and CDs, which management expects to ease as liquidity improves.
Q1 NIM hit by flow-through of end-March deposit costs, and by slippages and reduced recoveries; management says Q1 NIM is the worst case for the year.
Gold LTV around 75% vs peers below 65%, driven by agri gold (LTV up to 85%); non-agri LTV about 50%-55%. Board plans to gradually cut agri gold.
Deposit rates showing marginal softening; SME yields expected to improve next quarter as slippages are upgraded in Q2/Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Gold share at 54%, bulk deposits at 52% of term deposits; is the bulk mix the main NIM drag and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the bulk mix (about 52% of term deposits) raises cost of funds (about 6.5%). Retail franchise build starts with CASA from FY2028; management expects no quick reduction in bulk share in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Can a wholesale book funded by wholesale money hold margins, and how volatile are slippages?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NIM and ROA guidance holds for the year; wholesale is being built as a franchise with ROA and RAROC targets. Q1 slippage about Rs.98 Crores (Q4 about Rs.60 Crores), mainly in BLG/SME, which management expects to be largely upgraded in Q2/Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall 7%?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury profit was Rs.12 Crores vs Rs.53 Crores a year ago, insurance fees were cut after mis-selling controls, and gold/retail processing fees fell with lower disbursements. Management expects recovery from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 ROA guidance being revised from around 1.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it will not go below 1.3% for FY27, with an internal 1.5% target; the 1.3% comment answered a different question on the year-end run-rate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of IDBI Bank stake sale by promoter Fairfax?
qa_highlights.answer: CSB has had no discussions on this. Fairfax told management to continue business as usual; the bank is run by its own management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gold disbursements fall sharply QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited regulatory implementation (end-use monitoring), fewer top-ups as gold prices stopped rising, and the repledger LAS run-off. Disbursements are expected to pick up as gold prices rise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECLGS disbursement and what is the growth guidance for corporate and gold?
qa_highlights.answer: ECLGS disbursements about Rs.60 Crores so far. Management guided wholesale at 35%-40% growth and gold at 30%-35% for FY27.

risks_watch: Asset quality volatility: slippages of about Rs.98 Crores in Q1 vs Rs.60 Crores in Q4, concentrated in BLG/SME; upgrade assumption for Q2/Q3 is key.
Margin pressure from bulk and CD funding (cost of funds about 6.5%); the NIM path depends on deposit repricing and CD rates easing.
Other income recovery depends on treasury gains (AFS book) and insurance and gold fee pick-up from Q2.
Gold regulation: end-use monitoring and the gold mix glide path from 54% toward 30% by FY2030.
Execution of the CASA/retail franchise, with CASA ratio expected to hold at 19.41% only if deposits grow about 25%.
Management said Q1 ROA of 1.09% is below the FY27 guidance of 1.3%-1.5%, so the run-rate must improve materially in later quarters.
542867|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the year-on-year numbers and guidance, but defensive on the quarter-on-quarter dip in NIM, ROA and other income, which it attributes to transient factors. Management was also candid about the delayed technology decision and avoided commenting on the IDBI Bank stake sale beyond saying it was not involved.
key_quotes: We will only improve from here.
In 2027 itself we will touch 1.3%.
I do not see liquidity as a risk for us in the near term.

Except for the technology which got delayed by around two-and-a-half years which was a decision point and not an execution point - almost everything else we achieved the way we had given guidance to the markets.

rows.why: Deposits up 26% YoY vs industry 13.4% and advances up 24% vs industry 18.6%; FY27 guidance of wholesale growth 35-40% and gold 30-35%.

rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the bank is in a technology completion phase rather than a capacity build, and CD ratio is just under 90% with no capex plan stated.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 NIM at about 3.75% and ROA at 1.3-1.5%, and Q1 ROA of 1.09% is well below the 1.3% floor, so no upgrade is signalled.

rows.why: Q1 ROA of 1.09% is below the 1.3% FY27 floor and Q1 slippages rose to about Rs.98 Crores from Rs.60 Crores in Q4, so the run-rate must improve materially; if upgrades slip, the ROA floor is at risk.

rows.why: Trade, supply chain and CMS systems go live in the next 3-4 months, and a new retail liability acquisition channel is rolling out with retail deposit products launched last year; unsecured retail push is deferred to FY2028.

rows.label: SME/BLG slippage upgrades in Q2/Q3
rows.why: Q1 slippages of about Rs.98 Crores (Q4 about Rs.60 Crores) are expected to be largely upgraded in Q2/Q3, and SME yield fell to 9.25% from 9.81% QoQ, so NIM and asset quality recovery depends on this.

rows.label: Fee income recovery to 16-17% of total income
rows.why: Q1 other income was about 15% of income and treasury profit fell to Rs.12 Crores from Rs.53 Crores YoY; management expects insurance and gold fees to pick up from Q2.

rows.label: Repledger LAS run-off complete
rows.why: Repledger LAS book fell from over Rs.2,100 Crores to about Rs.60 Crores and will run off by next quarter under RBI discontinuation from 1 April 2026.

tone.note: Management was confident on YoY growth and FY27 NIM/ROA guidance and called Q1 the worst-case margin quarter, but defensive on the QoQ dip in NIM, ROA and other income; analysts pushed on ROA below the 1.3% floor, slippages, and the bulk-deposit cost drag.

542867|2026-09.headline: CSB Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose 22% QoQ to Rs.183 Cr, with NIM up to 3.81% and ROA to 1.29%.
542867|2026-09.overview: CSB Bank reported Q2 FY27 net profit of Rs.183 Cr, up 22% QoQ and 14% YoY, with net interest income of Rs.510 Cr (up 7% QoQ, 20% YoY). NIM widened to 3.81% from 3.66% in Q1, driven by a higher yield on advances (10.92%) and stable cost of funds. Fee income rebounded 20% QoQ, though overall fee income was down about 22% YoY due to market-linked non-core lines. Asset quality improved on GNPA (1.58%) and NNPA (0.33%), with credit cost at 24 bps, though elevated write-offs of fully provided card and unsecured book were flagged. Management said it is entering a "scale phase" with retail liability build-out, SME growth restarting, and guidance of ROA 1.5% to 1.8% next year.

financial_highlights.change: +20% QoQ; ex-treasury +27% QoQ; fee income -22% YoY
vs 3.66% in Q1 FY27 and 3.81% in Q2 FY26
Yield on advances 10.92% vs 10.65% in Q1
PCR 87.65% (79.19% without PWO); credit cost 24 bps

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book grew 36% YoY, but tonnage fell about 6% YoY and disbursements slowed; management targets gold at about 50% of loan mix by year-end (53% last year, 54% last quarter), with a 32% glide path by 2030. Gold yields rose about 50 bps QoQ.

segments.name: Corporate / wholesale
segments.commentary: Corporate segment grew 44% YoY; wholesale split roughly equally across corporate banking, mid-market and FIs, with corporate and mid-market growing faster.

segments.name: SME
segments.commentary: SME growth remained flattish after exits and customer losses on pricing; management expects SME growth to resume from this quarter after portfolio issues were corrected.

segments.name: Retail (ex-gold)
segments.commentary: Retail growth was muted; the bank degrew loan against security (repledge gold loans, now almost zero) and is keeping unsecured cards, agri and MFI cautious, with unsecured retail to restart around FY2028.

segments.name: Fee income
segments.commentary: Core fee grew about 27% YoY and is just short of 15% of total income; overall fee is just short of 17% of total income (vs 23% last year, which included one-offs). Non-core lines (PSLC, treasury) declined.

guidance_outlook: ROA this year expected between 1.30% and 1.5%; next year (FY28) targeted at 1.5% to 1.8%, closer to 1.5% initially.
NIM guided at around 3.75% to 3.8% this year; around 3.75% next year.
Cost of funds to be brought down from 6.55% to about 6% next financial year.
Fee to total income assumed at 17% to 18%; IRDAI corporate agency draft may cut this by 0.5% to 1%.
Balance sheet growth guided at 30% to 50% faster than the system; system growth was faster this quarter due to FCNR inflows.
CASA to grow faster than term deposits from FY2028, after being slower this year.
Gold loans to fall to about 50% of mix by year-end; SBS 2030 targets continue.
capex_capacity: Network of 872 branches and 844 ATMs as at September 2026.
Core system upgrade and DC-DR switch completed; OFSAA implementation under way.
Technology investments span transaction banking (supply chain, CMS, trade), OBDX, corporate net banking and corporate LOS.
Management plans to launch 3-4 retail liability products every quarter, with current account acquisition the current focus.
Opex up about 11% QoQ and about 3% YoY; other opex up 18% QoQ mainly on technology, plus distribution and infrastructure; staff cost up about 17% YoY.
demand_pricing: Gold disbursements fell as rebooking is no longer shown as new disbursement and gold prices dipped; management says the regulator's LTV cut from 90% to 75% was managed.
Gold loan LTV about 75% vs 60-65% at peers, attributed to a larger agri portfolio where higher LTV is allowed; about 28% of gold book is above Rs.20 lakh ticket size.
Gold yields raised by about 50 bps QoQ, leveraging distribution and competitor pricing.
Lost some SME customers on pricing; exited a list of customers after quality review.
Deposit mix about 48% retail and 52% wholesale; FCY, CDs and borrowings remain significant funding sources.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other opex rise 18% QoQ and is it linked to higher other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said total opex rose about 11% QoQ and 3% YoY; the rise was mainly technology, plus distribution expansion and infrastructure spends. Staff cost was up about 17% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp rise in yield on advances and gold yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Better asset quality, careful yield management in wholesale and SME, and a gold yield increase of about 50 bps QoQ, helped by distribution reach and competitor pricing. Cost of funds was flat QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Why were write-offs high while credit cost was low?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wrote off a fully provided vintage of credit card and unsecured loans with low recovery prospects and no PSL benefit; it said this had no impact on credit cost, which was 24 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the IRDAI corporate agency consultation paper on fees?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates a 0.5% to 1% drag on fee-to-income, so guidance may drop from 18% to 17% short term, with the bank aiming to recover through core fee lines.

qa_highlights.question: What is the balance sheet growth outlook and retail deposit traction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated growth 30% to 50% faster than system; retail current account acquisition has started, and liability franchise takes two to three years to build. Asset growth is not the constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Is Fairfax or IDBI relevant to CSB, and is there a Fairfax deposit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Fairfax has no deposits with the bank and the board has not discussed the Fairfax/IDBI matter; the transaction is still incomplete.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ROA and NIM outlooks for this year and next?
qa_highlights.answer: ROA of 1.30-1.5% this year, 1.5-1.8% next year; NIM around 3.75-3.8%, with cost of funds targeted at about 6% next year to offset mix shift.

risks_watch: Gold loan tonnage down about 6% YoY and gold disbursements slowing; gold book mix must fall to about 50%.
Regulatory fee risk from IRDAI corporate agency draft; fee-to-income could fall 0.5-1%.
Asset quality trend needs two to three more quarters to confirm; management points to a declining non-gold SMA book.
Cost of funds at 6.55% and reliance on FCY borrowings, CDs and bulk deposits; CASA ratio slipped to 18.96%.
Opex growth (other opex +18% QoQ) and cost-to-income at 64.8% against the fee and NIM outlook.
Interpretation risk on write-offs: elevated write-offs of fully provided book alongside PCR rising to 87.65%.
542867|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on earnings momentum, ROA and the scale phase, but guarded on the timing of retail growth, CASA recovery and the fee impact from the IRDAI draft. Management declined to elaborate on the other income breakup and deflected the Fairfax/IDBI question as not yet relevant.
key_quotes: Overall, we had a fairly good quarter.

We will start seeing the growth on the SME side from this quarter onwards because most of the portfolio-related issues we faced in SME book for the last one-and-a-half years have been by and large corrected now.
I would say that we would aim to bring down the cost of funds to somewhere around 6% next financial year, which will give us a 50-basis points lift.

rows.why: Network stands at 872 branches and 844 ATMs as at Sep 2026 with no new branch additions guided; growth is coming from balance sheet and liability products rather than new physical capacity.

rows.why: FY27 ROA guidance was narrowed to 1.30-1.50%, i.e. effectively a cut from prior implied range, and fee-to-income may fall 0.5-1% from IRDAI draft, so upward revisions look unlikely near term.

rows.why: FY27 ROA is guided 1.30-1.50% after a cut, fee-to-income could drop from 18% to 17% under the IRDAI corporate agency draft (0.5-1% drag), and cost-to-income is 64.8% with other opex up 18% QoQ.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans to launch 3-4 retail liability products every quarter, with current account acquisition already started, though unsecured retail (cards, agri, MFI) is only set to restart around FY2028.

rows.label: CASA growth turns faster than term deposits from FY28
rows.why: CASA ratio slipped to 18.96% and CASA grows slower than TDs this year, with management saying FY27 is the last year of that gap and cost of funds targeted at ~6% from 6.55%.

rows.label: SME growth restarts after portfolio clean-up
rows.why: SME growth was flattish after exits and pricing-driven customer losses; management expects it to resume from this quarter, but the asset quality trend needs two to three more quarters to confirm.

rows.label: IRDAI corporate agency draft fee impact
rows.why: Management estimates a 0.5% to 1% drag on fee-to-income, which would move guidance from 18% to about 17%.

tone.note: Management was confident on NIM, ROA trajectory and the scale phase, but cautious on gold tonnage, retail growth timing, CASA recovery and the IRDAI fee draft; analysts pushed on write-offs, other opex and the Fairfax/IDBI matter, which management deflected.

542904|2026-03.headline: Ujjivan SFB Q4FY26: Q4 PAT annualised to ROA 2.1%, but FY27 guidance of ~1.6% ROA, ~25% advances growth and 1.4-1.5% credit cost.
542904|2026-03.overview: Q4FY26 showed strong operating momentum: NII rose 26.4% YoY to INR1,092 crores, NIM improved to 8.5%, disbursements hit a record INR9,811 crores, and gross loan book reached INR40,655 crores (+26.6% YoY). Exit-quarter PAT was INR282 crores (ROA 2.1%, ROE 17.2%) versus FY26 PAT of INR693 crores (ROA 1.4%, ROE 10.9%). The RBI returned the bank's application for voluntary transition to a universal bank; management will reapply later with a more diversified portfolio. Management guided to a higher secured mix (about 56% by March 2027), a board-approved equity raise of up to INR2,000 crores in H2FY27, and FY27 ROA of around 1.6%, below the Q4 exit rate.

segments.name: Secured portfolio
segments.commentary: Reached INR20,079 crores (+43.5% YoY, +12.6% QoQ), now 49.4% of gross book. Housing +43.4% YoY and MSME +57.9% YoY; the housing vertical crossed INR10,000 crores.

segments.name: Micro banking
segments.commentary: Portfolio INR20,709 crores (+6.9%); Q4 disbursements a record INR5,245 crores (+11.9% QoQ). FY26 new customer additions 5.4 lakh. Management guides FY27 growth below 10%, a higher single digit.

segments.name: Newer lines (gold, vehicle, agri)
segments.commentary: Grew 292%, 102% and 127% YoY respectively; together about 6% of loan mix versus 3% in FY25. Gold yield is above 14%; micro mortgage yield is 19.7%.

segments.name: Liabilities
segments.commentary: Retail TD plus CASA INR31,955 crores (70% of deposits). CD ratio 89%, LCR 142%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 advances growth around 25%: secured about 40% and unsecured about 10%, per the Chief Credit Officer.
FY27 credit cost moderates to 1.4-1.5% of average GLB (exit quarter DuPont credit cost about 1.1%, per the call).
FY27 ROA around 1.6%, base case, with upside possible; NIM guided at around 8.5%, in line with the Q4 exit level.
Opex to ATA 20-30bps above FY26 in FY27 due to investment, then expected to decline; cost to income to stay at FY26 levels.
Secured share about 56% by March 2027. CASA ratio about 29-30% (Head of Retail Liabilities said around 30%).

Equity raise up to INR2,000 crores, planned for H2FY27. About 20% branch addition in FY27 (about 140 branches on 776 base). Cost of deposits to benefit about 25-30bps from SA rate cuts; no TD repricing planned.
capex_capacity: Branch network 776 as of March 2026; FY27 plan to add about 20% (about 140 branches, confirmed by management as broadly yes).
Digital, AI and analytics investment on a cloud-led data platform; the spend is driving the opex increase.
Equity raise up to INR2,000 crores, to maintain buffer over the Board-mandated 20% CAR threshold and fund growth for about 3 years.
No inorganic acquisition of secured book is planned.
demand_pricing: Industry bank credit grew 16% to INR219 lakh crore and deposits 13.4% to INR268 lakh crore as of March 31, 2026.
Management cut SA rates in April; expects a 25-30bps reduction in SA cost of funds. SA exit cost of funds was 5.21% in March.
No plan to reprice retail or bulk TDs or MFI yields; management is watching competitors who have raised TD rates.
Gold ticket size rose about 60% YoY, with yields up about 30bps QoQ after lowering rates on small tickets.
Management said deposit growth will match credit growth; a slowdown in deposits in the July-August period was deliberate because of excess liquidity.
MFI slippages for Q4 around INR130 crores; Bucket-X collection efficiency 99.8% in March 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why does ROA fall from about 2% to 1.6% if NIM, opex and credit cost are flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is conservative on opex and credit cost and covers possible stress in a couple of key products; no specific line item was identified. It will update if the number changes materially.

qa_highlights.question: Will the secured mix shift cut yields and margins, and how much cost-of-funds benefit is left?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30bps of deposit repricing benefit remains. Management cites 2-wheeler, gold (above 14%) and micro mortgage (19.7%) yields to offset lower housing and MSME yields. NIM guided at about 8.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise equity when CAR is already strong?
qa_highlights.answer: The asset growth guidance is 25% a year against a Board threshold of 20%, and the bank needs growth capital for about 3 years. The raise is planned for H2FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why not grow MFI faster, with a larger share of new customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Most FY26 acquired customers are not yet eligible for repeat loans, so growth will be mostly repeat-driven. New-to-bank share is about 25%, possibly rising to 30%, but not 40-45%, which would be too risky.

qa_highlights.question: What is the secured mix target and reapplication timeline for universal bank status?
qa_highlights.answer: The RBI gives no ratio. Management expects about 56% secured by March 2027, and the reapplication timeline will be set after a 2-3 year plan, not immediately.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a contingency provision buffer for ECL or universal bank readiness in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No, management has no plan for additional provisions in FY27 beyond the guidance.

Deposit competition: peers have raised TD rates; the bank has no plan to match, so CASA and TD growth need watching.
Micro banking growth held below 10% as repeat-loan-driven; watch the 5.4 lakh new-customer run-rate and any guardrail changes.

West Asia conflict and oil price exposure: management says the book has no FX lending and no oil, gas, defence or aviation exposure, but is tightening 2-wheeler, used vehicle and MSME working capital monitoring.
Equity raise timing (H2FY27) and dilution; universal bank reapplication timeline still undefined.

542904|2026-06.headline: Ujjivan SFB Q1 FY27 PAT rose to INR317 crore (ROA 2.2%, ROE 18.2%); FY27 ROA guidance raised to 1.8-2.0%.
542904|2026-06.overview: Gross loans reached INR42,903 crore (+28.9% YoY, +5.5% QoQ) and deposits INR48,129 crore (+25% YoY), with CASA up 37.8% YoY to INR12,930 crore. Net interest income was INR1,186 crore with NIM stable at 8.5%, and GNPA fell 10 bps to 2.17% with PCR at 85%. Management revised FY27 credit cost guidance to 0.9-1.0% of average total assets and raised ROA guidance to 1.8-2.0%, helped by deferred capacity-building spend (about INR250 crore planned for FY27, mostly from June onward) and lower opex (now about 6.4% of average assets).

segments.name: Micro banking (MFI)
segments.commentary: Book INR21,371 crore (+16.8% YoY), disbursements INR4,581 crore (+16.4% YoY). Bucket X collection efficiency 99.68%; slippages annualised about 1.72% vs 2.68% in Q4; provision coverage about 95%.

segments.name: Affordable housing and micro mortgages
segments.commentary: Combined gross book INR11,210 crore (+40.8% YoY). GNPA stable at 1.2% (affordable housing) and 0.6% (micro mortgages). Micro mortgage book about INR1,800 crore, yield about 19.5%, PAR rising from about 1.2% to 1.5%.

segments.name: Secured book
segments.commentary: Secured book INR21,638 crore (+42.7% YoY, +7.8% QoQ), now 50.4% of loans.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Book INR3,470 crore (+54% YoY); new book GNPA 0.5%; MSME PAR down 13 bps. Ticket sizes rising, with LAP at INR80-90 lakh and working capital at INR1.1-1.2 crore; disbursement yield expected around 10.5%.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Book INR1,020 crore (+248.6% YoY); Q1 disbursements INR467 crore (+183.9% YoY). Sourced from 455 branches (106 added in the quarter); origination LTV 75%, book LTV about 56%.

segments.name: Vehicle loans
segments.commentary: Book INR1,036 crore (+85.1% YoY), GNPA 1.7%, served through 337 branches with a mid-premium and EV focus. New lines (gold, vehicle, agri) are 7% of the loan book and 9% of Q1 disbursements.

guidance_outlook: FY27 ROA guidance raised to 1.8-2.0% (from the earlier guidance), citing opex and credit cost.
FY27 credit cost guidance revised to 0.9-1.0% of average total assets (earlier basis: average gross loan book); credit cost was 0.9% in Q1.
FY27 opex expected at about 6.4% of average assets, lower than earlier plan, as capacity spend (about INR250 crore) is deferred to later quarters.
FY27 planned asset growth of 25% reaffirmed.
Target of 56% secured loan mix by March 2027 maintained.
Bulk deposit ratio to stay around 30%; no immediate further deposit rate hikes seen, with marginal cost-of-funds increase expected.
Opex to decline year-on-year in FY28 as investment intensity eases.

qa_highlights.question: Can yields be sustained in affordable housing and non-MFI segments, and is 2% ROA possible on a steady-state basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Affordable housing yield around 12.5% with ticket INR16-20 lakh and about 580-590 branches; some competitive pressure but yields maintained. Micro mortgage yields about 19.5%, and yields do not fall much at INR10-12 lakh tickets.

qa_highlights.question: Will cost of funds rise further, and is any more deposit rate hike needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Brajesh Cherian said no immediate upward revision is needed, only a marginal increase in cost of funds is expected, and this is built into the 1.8-2.0% ROA guidance. IBPC, refinance and securitisation are available.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity-building spend and does the guidance embed NIM compression?
qa_highlights.answer: Bala Kamath said about INR250 crore planned, with little spent in Q1 and spend starting in June; the 1.8-2.0% ROA guidance includes it. NIM guidance given at the start of the year is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the credit cost guidance cut and are there early warning signs in MFI?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Goel said MFI bucket X collection efficiency is 99.7% and July trends are similar; Q1 MFI slippages annualised about 1.72% vs 2.68% in Q4. Each 5-7 bps move in collections would only marginally change credit cost.

qa_highlights.question: What is the micro mortgage PAR and LGD outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: PAR rose from about 1.2% to about 1.5%; GNPA from about 0.47% to about 0.55%. Management says 18 and 24 MOB vintages have not exceeded about 2.5% and the book is still maturing; bucket X collection is 99.7-99.75%.

qa_highlights.question: How will opex trend after FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex is 6.4% of average assets in FY27; Sadananda Kamath said FY28 investment will be lower and opex will improve year-on-year, with exact figures to follow.

capex_capacity: Capacity-building spend planned at about INR250 crore for FY27; per management, little was spent in Q1 and spending started in June (marketing, IT, branch openings), building up over coming quarters.

Branch network at 814 as of June 2026 after 38 new branches in Q1; plan to add 144 branches in FY27 (106 yet to open). Gold loan active branches to rise from about 430-440 to about 575 by end-FY27; gold disbursement exit rate targeted at INR230-250 crore a month by March 2027 (June exit about INR170-175 crore a month).

Affordable housing capacity built at about INR350-375 crore disbursement a month; micro mortgage disbursement about INR100 crore a month, expected to reach INR140-150 crore by March 2027. Incremental book mix tilts toward micro mortgages.
Opex guided at about 6.4% of average assets for FY27; management expects FY28 opex to decline year-on-year as investment intensity eases.

New products: Unsecured Fast Track loan ready to scale after pilot; pre-owned car loans piloted in Karnataka, to test in 2-3 geographies this year; mid-corporate lending started in Q1; purchase invoice discounting added to MSME suite; co-branded credit card in testing. HCV/LCV only after FY27.
demand_pricing: Gross loans INR42,903 crore (+28.9% YoY, +5.5% QoQ); disbursements INR9,245 crore (+41.4% YoY). Secured book INR21,638 crore, 50.4% of loans.

Micro banking book INR21,371 crore (+16.8% YoY), disbursements INR4,581 crore (+16.4% YoY); 1.72 lakh new customers in Q1. Management says demand is rising across almost all states; Kerala deliberately not being grown.
Affordable housing and micro mortgages INR11,210 crore (+40.8% YoY). Micro mortgage book about INR1,800 crore at ~19.5% yield; affordable housing yield about 12.5%, ticket INR16-20 lakh.

MSME book INR3,470 crore (+54% YoY). LAP ticket moved from INR58-60 lakh to INR80-90 lakh; working capital from INR70-80 lakh to INR1.1-1.2 crore. Disbursement yield expected around 10.5% vs earlier 11-11.5%, and below book yield.
Gold loans INR1,020 crore (+248.6% YoY); Q1 disbursement INR467 crore; monthly disbursement averaged INR160-170 crore in Q1. Vehicle loans INR1,036 crore (+85.1% YoY).

Deposits INR48,129 crore (+25% YoY); CASA INR12,930 crore (+37.8% YoY). Bulk deposit ratio about 30%, retail TD now said to be cheaper than bulk TD. Rates raised in June on key buckets; no immediate further hike seen. FCNR(B) raised about INR60 crore in Q1.
Cost of funds 6.86%, continuing to fall. Management sees only marginal increase ahead; no further repricing benefit visible. NIM stable at 8.5%; FY27 NIM guidance unchanged per management.
Competition: management acknowledged competitive pressure in affordable housing and CASA mobilisation and pricing pressure across asset products, but says yields are being held.
risks_watch: Deposit competition and CASA mobilisation: management flagged tight liquidity and deposit pressure; cost of funds may tick up marginally despite no further repricing benefit.
Yield pressure as ticket sizes rise in MSME (disbursement yield about 10.5%, below book yield) and affordable housing faces competition.
Monsoon and kharif sowing: management flagged El Nino and kharif delays as a key H2 monitorable; credit cost guidance relies on stable MFI collections.
Micro mortgage PAR rising (about 1.2% to 1.5%); management expects a natural increase as the book matures, so this needs monitoring.
Execution risk on the INR250 crore capacity spend and the 144-branch plan, which must lift deposits to fund the 25% asset growth; FY27 ROA guidance of 1.8-2.0% relies on it.
key_quotes: Our strategy continues to remain centered on strengthening our liability franchise, building a diversified asset portfolio and maintaining prudent risk management practices to ensure profitability along with growth.
This deferred commencement of expenses, coupled with ongoing efficiency gains will result in full year opex to be lower than earlier planned and now would be around 6.4% of average assets.
We are pleased to note that our progress towards diversification of loan portfolio remains on track with more than half of the loan book being secured at 50.4% as of June '26.

We remain mindful of the prevailing funding rate environment and the continued competitive intensity in CASA mobilization, along with pricing pressures across key asset products and the resulting impact on margins.

More cautious on liabilities, where management said deposit pressure is present and rate moves are being watched; it declined to give vertical-level profitability or product ROA.

542904|2026-09.headline: Ujjivan SFB posted record quarterly PAT of INR365 crores (ROA 2.4%, ROE 19.7%) in Q2 FY27, with deposits up 29.2% to INR50,643 crores.
542904|2026-09.overview: Ujjivan SFB reported strong Q2 FY27 growth: gross loans rose 32.1% YoY to INR45,699 crores and NII rose 35% YoY to INR1,244 crores, with NIM at 8.4%. Asset quality was stable, with GNPA at 2.1%, NNPA at 0.3%, and a credit cost of 0.7%. Management guided NIM down about 10 bps to around 8.35% in H2 after the 25 bps repo hike, and flagged that ROA could overshoot the guided range. The MD's early retirement is pending a successor, and a preferential equity raise of INR409 crores is subject to shareholder approval.

segments.name: Micro banking (unsecured)
segments.commentary: Book INR22,037 crores, grew about 6% in H1 FY27; FY27 guidance of 12-14% reiterated. Bucket X collection efficiency 99.7%; about 2 lakh customers added in Q2.

segments.name: Affordable housing
segments.commentary: Book INR10,056 crores, crossed INR10,000 crores; GNPA 1.2%, PAR 3.7%; ticket size about INR17.9 lakh; growth about 37-38% on OSP.

segments.name: Micro mortgage
segments.commentary: Book INR2,031 crores, up 85.7% YoY; GNPA 0.7%; PAR around 1.8%, expected to settle at 2.5% to just below 3%.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Book INR3,871 crores, up 51.3% YoY; new book above INR3,000 crores with GNPA 0.5%. Operates in top 50 cities, South the largest region.

segments.name: Gold loan
segments.commentary: Book INR1,275 crores, up 209.8% YoY; 117 branches added in H1, similar number planned for H2; disbursement LTV below 78%.

segments.name: Agri banking and 2-wheeler
segments.commentary: Agri book INR914 crores (+79.2% YoY); 2-wheeler loans INR1,081 crores (+64.8% YoY).

segments.name: Insurance / TPP
segments.commentary: Insurance income about INR90 crores in H1; about 50% from credit life. TPP grew 41% QoQ and 30% YoY. IRDAI commission norms are a draft; submissions due October 25.

guidance_outlook: NIM expected to fall about 10 bps to around 8.35% in H2 FY27, from the 25 bps repo hike, partly offset by planned DA changes.
Opex to ATA ratio now seen at about 6.2% versus earlier 6.4% guidance; part of brand spend spills into Q3.
Credit cost in H2 expected in line with H1 (about 0.8%), within the 90-100 bps guided range per the company's stated range; management said H2 run rate equals H1.
ROA could overshoot the upper end of the guided range; management said a significant beat looks highly probable.
Microfinance growth guided at 12-14% for FY27; affordable housing growth about 35% in plan.
Secured share of book at 52% targeted to reach 56% by end FY27, rising about 5% each year.

CASA ratio expected to be about 2 percentage points below the 30% level by year end, per Hitendra Jha.

Gold loan branches: 117 added in H1, similar number planned for H2.
Brand campaign launched September 2026 with new ambassador R. Madhavan; spend to reflect in H2 with spillover into Q3.
Digital and technology institution-building spends to reflect in H2 at a slower pace than planned.
Securitization pool increased by INR500 crores in October 2026; described as NIM accretive and P&L neutral.
demand_pricing: Micro banking new customer acquisition rose sequentially with about 2 lakh customers added in Q2; NTB up 34% YoY.
Karnataka book INR2,400 crores, of which only INR15.1 crores is eligible under SLBC drought norms; Maharashtra MFI book INR1,682 crores, with SLBC-eligible agri loans of only INR18 crores.
Management said drought-related government intervention is not yet affecting collections; September collections were about 99.7%.
Individual loan ticket size around INR1.5 lakh is the comfort level; micro mortgage ticket size rising to about INR7.5-7.8 lakh, targeted to stabilize near INR8 lakh.
Deposit growth led by HNI, NR, corporate salary segments and top 80 and top 30 cities, where CASA growth is about 40%.
MDR on UPI payments deferred until after Diwali; if implemented, management expects income upside with no added expense.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins move in H2 FY27 and FY28 given the steeper rate cycle and the secured mix shift?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said NIM would fall to about 8.35% in H2 from 8.45% in Q2, with a 10 bps impact from the 25 bps repo hike; mix impact offset by planned DA changes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the drought in Karnataka and Maharashtra on collections and credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said credit cost lags by about 6 months and will stay within the guided range. Agri and allied exposure is limited, and Bucket X collection efficiency is 99.7%; microfinance guidance of 12-14% is intact.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the opex budget of about INR250 crores will be spent this year, and is extra provisioning planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex to ATA now seen at about 6.2% versus 6.4% earlier. Siddharth Bharadwaj said H2 credit cost run rate matches H1, with no increase planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for CASA and deposit mobilization?
qa_highlights.answer: Hitendra Jha said CASA growth moderated due to some temporary outflows and that NTB rose 34% YoY. The company will make calibrated SA and retail TD rate revisions; CASA is expected to be about 2 percentage points below 30%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company revise full-year ROA guidance upward?
qa_highlights.answer: Siddharth Bharadwaj said a significant beat on the upper end of ROA guidance looks highly probable, citing opex at 6.2% of ATA.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the balance equity raise and the MD succession?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the balance of the INR2,000 crore approval will be raised before the resolution expires in July 2027. The NRC aims to complete the MD search in 3 to 4 months from September 1.

risks_watch: Interim CEO status: MD Sanjeev Nautiyal retired early for health reasons; successor search targeted to finish in 3-4 months from September 1.
IRDAI draft on insurance commissions (about 50% of insurance income is credit-life linked); final guidelines and submissions due October 25 are pending.
Drought in Karnataka and Maharashtra, and the broader monsoon risk; PAR trend in group and micro mortgage books inching up.
Repo hike pass-through to cost of funds; management guided to upward cost of funds from Q3.

Balance of fundraise (about INR1,591 crores of the INR2,000 crore approval) still to be raised before July 2027.

542905|2026-03.headline: Hindware FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 27% to ₹233 crore on 9% margin, while Q4 revenue fell to ₹663 crore from ₹699 crore.
542905|2026-03.overview: Consolidated FY26 revenue was ₹2,510 crore (flat vs ₹2,523 crore), with EBITDA up 27% to ₹233 crore and margin at 9% vs 7%. Q4 revenue fell 5% YoY to ₹663 crore, but EBITDA rose 23% to ₹63 crore and PBT before exceptional items was ₹15 crore vs ₹2 crore. Bathware grew 10% in FY26 with margins up 160 bps, while pipes revenue declined and posted a PBT loss, with a March resin-price spike cutting inventory and sales. Home Innovation (consumer appliances) is being rationalised, with management guiding to EBITDA-positive in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Bathware (sanitaryware and faucets)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹1,520 crore (+10%), EBITDA ₹157 crore, margin 10.3% (+160 bps). Q4 revenue +10% with tile supply shortfalls; management says tiles non-availability cost about 2-3% of growth in Q4.

segments.name: Pipes
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹673 crore with PBT loss of ₹29 crore; management described FY26 as challenging. Q4 PBT loss of ₹10 crore reflected March resin-driven supply shortfall; April reportedly grew about 50% YoY.

segments.name: Home Innovation (consumer appliances)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹317 crore with EBITDA of negative ₹12 crore; Q4 revenue ₹80 crore and EBITDA negative ₹7 crore. Loss-making categories such as air coolers (except e-commerce), ceiling and other fans, air purifiers, water purifiers and furniture fittings are being discontinued.

guidance_outlook: Bathware: FY27 growth of 15-20% (value), with margin expansion of 1-2% YoY in FY27 and another 1-2% in FY28; management says it will reach the teens margin within two years.
Pipes: volume growth of about 14-15% expected; management said margins may improve as resin stabilises around ₹80-85/kg, but gave no margin guidance. Second half of FY27 expected stronger than first.
Pipes margin: consolidated (console) margin expansion of 1.5-2% per year for at least the next 2 years, per Sandeep Sikka.

542907|2026-03.headline: Prince Pipes Q4 FY26 revenue rose 18% to INR850 crore and EBITDA doubled to INR110 crore on 23% volume growth; management guides 11-13% margin.
542907|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered record quarterly volumes of 62,167 MT (+23% YoY), with revenue of INR850 crore (+18%) and EBITDA of INR110 crore (+100%, 13% margin). Management attributed the quarter to aggressive pricing, pass-through of inventory gains to channel partners, product mix (CPVC, PPR) and absence of inventory losses, which had hurt the first nine months. FY26 revenue grew 3% to INR2,598 crore, volume rose 8% and EBITDA rose 43% to INR232 crore (9% margin). Management guided to 11-13% annual EBITDA margin and 12-15% annual volume growth, while flagging April destocking and a weak channel in April before a May revival.

542907|2026-06.headline: Prince Pipes Q1 FY27 revenue rose 5% to INR 609 crore and EBITDA jumped 93% to INR 77 crore (13% margin) despite a 7% volume decline.

Management attributed the margin gain mainly to a better product mix (less agri, more plumbing; more CPVC/PPR versus PVC) and better realisations, while April was a destocking washout after a PVC price correction when import duty was suspended. Management said June and July saw recovery in channel restocking, and it reiterated FY27 guidance of 12-15% volume growth and 11-13% EBITDA margin. Inventory days rose to 100, which management attributed to supply insecurity during the war and a volume shortfall, and it expects normalisation to 65-75 days by end-September quarter.

Management said inventory costs normalised by end-Q2 and guided to normal H2 margins, while flagging H2 as challenging due to El Nino and low reservoir levels.

543064|2026-06.headline: Cohance Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell 23% YoY to INR4,223 million and adjusted EBITDA margin dropped to 2.2%, with management guiding to a Q2 sequential rebound.

Adjusted EBITDA of INR92 million and gross margin of 71.5% (vs 73%) reflected negative operating leverage. Management also laid out an integrated nucleic acid business under Dr. P.Y. Reddy with a path to full Sapala ownership by FY30, and disclosed a USFDA Form 483 with five observations at Pashamylaram.

543066|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 PAT rose 14% YoY to INR609 crore on lower credit cost (7.7%), though FY27 cost-to-income guided at 55-58%.
543066|2026-03.overview: SBI Cards reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR5,187 crore (+7% YoY) and PAT of INR609 crore (+14% YoY), helped by gross credit cost falling 55 bps QoQ to 7.7% and GNPA down 46 bps QoQ to 2.41%. Receivables grew only about 2% YoY to INR56,926 crore, and management declined to guide on asset growth, tying it to card acquisition. FY26 PAT was INR2,167 crore (+13% YoY), with cost-to-income at 55.3% for the year after higher corporate-spend passback costs. Management expects revolver rates to drift down and is leaning on instalment lending to offset.

financial_highlights.change: management overlay retained at INR220 crore

segments.name: Card acquisition
segments.commentary: 917,000 new accounts added in Q4 against a 0.9-1.0 million quarterly target; FY26 sourcing mix 54% open market and 46% banca. Management said next quarter is expected in a similar range.

segments.name: Spends
segments.commentary: Q4 total spends above INR1.15 trillion (+31% YoY); retail spends INR89,786 crore (+13% YoY). FY26 total spends INR4.3 trillion, retail INR3.54 trillion (+15%). Online share of retail spends 62.5% in FY26; spend market share 18.1%.

segments.name: Receivables and revolve
segments.commentary: Receivables INR56,926 crore (~+2% YoY). Interest-earning assets 54%, revolver balance 22%; revolve rate has been 22-24% over two years with a slight downward bias expected in FY27.

543066|2026-09.headline: SBI Card Q2 FY27 PAT rose 75% YoY to INR778 crore on lower credit costs, while spend growth was just 3% and NIM is guided range-bound around 10.8%.
543066|2026-09.overview: SBI Card reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of INR5,141 crore (up 4% YoY) and PAT of INR778 crore (up 75% YoY), driven mainly by lower credit costs. Gross credit cost fell to 5.6% (down 98 bps QoQ and 342 bps YoY) and gross NPA to 1.9%. Total spends grew about 3% YoY to INR1,10,689 crore, with retail spends up 6% to a record INR95,299 crore, and management attributed the weak headline to festive timing shifting into Q3. 543213|2026-03.headline: Rossari Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record Rs 684.9 crore (+18% YoY), but FY26 EBITDA margin fell to 11.9% from 12.7%.

March saw raw material price increases of 25-30% that compressed gross margin, and management says these are now being passed through from April. rows.why: Margin guide of 12-13% depends on pass-through holding in textiles and on pharma initiatives; FY26 margin already fell to 11.9% from 12.7%, and institutional/B2C losses have breakeven only targeted for FY27.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Pharma is a new focus area expected to carry the highest gross margin once scaled, with an FY27 pharma facility and aroma chemicals project in the Rs 50-75 crore capex, and AHN premix revenue ramp from Q1 FY27.

rows.label: Debt-free in ~18 months (aim)
rows.why: Management targets becoming debt-free within 18 months but said 'the time will tell'; capex cut to Rs 50-75 crore for FY27 frees cash, while divestment of non-core office space has no committed value or timeline (one to two years).

rows.label: Institutional and B2C breakeven in FY27
rows.why: Management expects breakeven or profitability in FY27 with losses moderating in H2 FY26, but B2C revenue is only Rs 250-260 crore on about 90 days of working capital and the target is not yet demonstrated.

rows.label: Raw material pass-through from April 2026
rows.why: Raw materials rose 25-30% in March and management says increases are being passed through from April 1, easy for most products but resisted in textiles, the key test for the 12-13% margin guide.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the Q4 record and the at-least-15% FY27 growth target, but cautious on the Middle East and raw material environment and the 12-13% margin; analysts pushed on the capex cut, the Reliance EO timing, segment margins and divestment values, which management left vague.

543213|2026-06.headline: Rossari Q1 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to Rs 697.2 crore, a record, but EBITDA margin slipped to 11.6% from 12.5%.
543213|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached Rs 697.2 crore (up 28% YoY) and EBITDA hit a record Rs 80.6 crore (up 18.7%), though margin fell to 11.6% from 12.5%. Core B2B EBITDA was Rs 85 crore (up 13%, ~14% margin), with the institutional and B2C businesses dragging margins and remaining flat in growth. PAT was Rs 35.1 crore (up 4.5%). Management is pursuing non-core asset monetisation, B2C exits and product-mix changes, and says Rs 11.6% is the margin base; target is ~15% EBITDA margin in about two years. Raw material spikes, phenol losses of about Rs 5 crore and freight volatility weighed on the quarter.

segments.name: HPPC
segments.commentary: Crossed Rs 550 crore quarterly revenue, growing ~28% YoY; new products such as NMMO, MDEA, spray-cooled powders, biosurfactants and fibre finishes are contributing.

segments.name: Textile Specialty Chemicals (TSC)
segments.commentary: Grew ~28% YoY; new Fibre Chemicals Division launched during the quarter.

segments.name: Animal Health and Nutrition (AHN)
segments.commentary: Grew ~28% YoY; vitamin premix plant now operational; trace minerals and enzyme premixes added. Pharma revenue was above Rs 50 crore last year and is guided to Rs 70-75 crore this year.

segments.name: Institutional and B2C
segments.commentary: Growth flat YoY; losses moderated. Institutional EBITDA margin cited at 13.6% vs ~16% last year. Debt in this business about Rs 50 crore; exit of consumer/B2C portion planned, institutional cleaning retained.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth of around 15% reiterated on an annualised basis, though management said quarterly prediction is becoming difficult.
Management says 11.6% EBITDA margin should be the base level; steady-state EBITDA margin target of at least 15%, expected in about two years.
Pharma revenue potential of Rs 30-50 crore in the second half of FY27 (Q2/Q3 compliance target), per analyst question on the Rs 70-75 crore figure.
Finance cost guided at Rs 9-10 crore per quarter run-rate going forward (Q1 interest about Rs 11 crore).
EO supply expected by around December 2026; FY28 expected to be better with a full year of additional EO.
Saudi Arabia project: about 1.5 years to first production after announcement; mix of EO and non-EO products; still in survey and feedstock/land allocation stage.
capex_capacity: India capex slowed to calibrated spend; only R&D-stage new molecules (pharma, aroma chemicals) to proceed; no large spend intended this year or next.

New R&D centre commissioned in Q4 FY26 and ramping up.

Saudi Arabia: initial operational and pre-operational spends only; capex not finalised.
demand_pricing: Volume grew ~10% YoY; balance of growth from higher pricing.
Pass-through of raw material price increases is achieved, but frequent up/down moves create buyer uncertainty; freight and vessel availability cost margin.
Phenol loss of about Rs 5 crore in Q4 FY26 due to delayed China shipments (noted as Q1 context by management); one-off RM block purchase also hurt the quarter; prices now back to earlier levels.
Growth shifted to non-EO products (esters, NMMO, NMM, NFM); agro demand subdued but non-EO agro inputs grew.
Single EO supplier in India, priced on world EO price; limited negotiating power.
Freight rates rose again after brief easing; new orders taken at higher freight.

qa_highlights.question: What margin improvement path and timing for EBITDA margin, given flat margins over 4-5 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Ketan Sablok said 11.6% is close to last quarter and slightly below last year; margins to improve as utilisation rises, low-margin exits and pharma/aroma mix shift. Wait-and-see for at least two quarters due to pricing and RM pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Is 11.6% the base margin and what is steady-state?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 11.6% should be the base level. Base business ex-B2C is 14-15%; target is around 15% steady-state EBITDA margin within two years after B2C recalibration and asset monetisation.

qa_highlights.question: Exit of B2C business: investment, debt and margin effect?
qa_highlights.answer: No separate investment as assets are shared (Silvassa). Debt in institutional/B2C about Rs 50 crore. Exit releases at least 2-3% EBITDA margin. Institutional cleaning retained; only consumer/B2C exits.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing vs volume growth and growth levers without EO availability?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume ~10% YoY, rest from pricing. Growth from new non-EO products (esters, NMMO, NMM, NFM), trace minerals, vitamin and enzyme premixes; pharma to rise to Rs 70-75 crore this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did domestic-focused peers gain while Rossari did not?
qa_highlights.answer: Single-molecule producers benefited; specialty players absorbed raw material hits. Phenol shipment delay from China cost about Rs 5 crore in the prior quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Saudi Arabia project timeline and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Survey and feedstock/land allocation still in progress; nothing finalised. About 1.5 years to first production after announcement; mix of EO and non-EO products.

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost rise and average cost of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher interest because term loans for capex were capitalised earlier and are now expensed as assets commissioned; run-rate to be Rs 9-10 crore per quarter.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on B2C exits, asset monetisation and utilisation; management declined to guide quarterly numbers.
EO supply (single Indian supplier) expected only by about December 2026; EO-linked growth is delayed.
Raw material and freight volatility linked to West Asia/geopolitics; freight rates rose again after easing.
Thailand and Saudi Arabia ramp-up and pre-operative costs weigh on margins.
Pharma compliance timeline (Q2/Q3) gates the Rs 30-50 crore H2 revenue potential.
Interest costs rising as capitalised projects go into P&L; watch whether run-rate falls to Rs 9-10 crore.
