543213|2026-09.headline: Rossari Q2 FY27 revenue rose 19% YoY to Rs 697.6 crore, a record, with EBITDA of Rs 87 crore (12.5% margin).
543213|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 set record revenue (Rs 697.6 crore, +19% YoY) and EBITDA (Rs 87 crore, +21% YoY), with growth led by volume and value-added products. Gross margin was 31.6%, up about 200 bps QoQ on product mix, but core B2B EBITDA margin fell to 14.1% from 14.8% YoY on freight and raw material costs. Management guided FY27 EBITDA margin to about 12% and revenue growth to mid-to-high teens, while citing uncertainty from the Middle East situation. Net debt fell to Rs 221 crore and working capital days improved to 86 from 97 at FY26 end.

segments.name: HPPC (Home, Personal Care & Industrial)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 541.9 crore, +18% YoY; H1 Rs 1,095.1 crore, +20% (H1 growth 24% per Sunil Chari). Growth led by personal care, agro surfactants, adjuvants and oil & gas; ethylene oxide constraints limited ethoxylate volumes and sequential revenue was broadly flat.

segments.name: Textile Specialty Chemicals
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 120.8 crore, +26% YoY and about +14% QoQ; H1 Rs 226.9 crore, +24%. Driven by exports to Bangladesh, Southeast Asia, Turkey and Latin America, plus the Thailand facility and the new fibre chemicals division.

segments.name: Animal Health & Nutrition (AHN)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 34.8 crore, +11% YoY; H1 Rs 72.8 crore, +19%. Q2 is seasonally the weakest quarter; management expects Q3 and Q4 to peak.

segments.name: Core B2B (ex institutional and B2C)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 619.9 crore, +21% YoY; EBITDA Rs 87.2 crore, +15% YoY, margin 14.1% vs 14.8% in Q2 FY26 and 13.5% in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Institutional and B2C
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 77.7 crore, +3% YoY; EBITDA +Rs 0.2 crore vs loss of Rs 3.7 crore in Q2 FY26, after portfolio rationalisation. Management targets positive EBITDA in H2 and for full FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 12% plus/minus; management expects margin improvement only from FY28.
FY27 revenue growth guided at mid-teens to high-teens, down from the 12-14% initial view, given demand and logistics uncertainty.
Peak utilisation of the new ethoxylation facility at Dahej expected about 2 years after commissioning, around end-FY28; peak sales target remains 3x capex value.
Working capital days expected to stay in the 87-90 day range by end-March 2027.
Working capital debt expected to be repaid by about mid-2027; all cash flows to go to debt reduction for now.
Exports targeted at 30%+ of revenue by end of this year (Q2 export share 31%, H1 27%).
capex_capacity: Blended capacity utilisation about 60%; new ethoxylation facility (Dahej) at about 30% and ramping; full healthy utilisation expected by next year as Reliance EO capacity arrives.
Reliance ethylene oxide expansion expected in Q1 FY28; no confirmed incremental EO allocation yet, with confirmation hoped for in the next couple of months.
Capital work in progress was Rs 156 crore at 30 September; about Rs 50-75 crore more capex in H2 FY27, with most projects closing by end-2026 and no major capex in India in the following year.
Remaining projects cover pharma excipients, aroma chemicals, hydrogenation and biosurfactant expansion; no volume figures disclosed yet.

Saudi Arabia: Board approved leasing land to wholly owned subsidiary Rossari International Limited Company for a greenfield plant; early site work (fencing, boundary wall) in coming months. Project details, capex and timelines to come after Board approval, likely in 8-12 months.
Thailand blending facility ramping up for Southeast Asia customers; EXCiPACT registration obtained for the Unitop plant.
demand_pricing: Q2 growth was mostly volume-driven; some product prices were cut as raw material prices eased early in the quarter.
Freight costs roughly doubled to tripled versus last year; not all customers absorb the full freight increase. Phenol and other core raw materials are higher YoY.
Export revenue grew about 34% YoY and about 35% QoQ in Q2; export share 31% of revenue; H1 export share 27%.
Pharma exports were about Rs 50 crore last year; qualification takes 6 months to 2 years, and management expects strong growth this year.
Oil and gas focus markets are India, the Middle East, and Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan; US sales go through distributors with no segment data.
Management declined to give a specific H2 revenue outlook, citing the Middle East situation, shipping routes and container and ISO tank availability.

qa_highlights.question: Where is export growth coming from and what is the export outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Export revenue grew about 34% YoY and 35% QoQ, driven by HPPC and textiles in Southeast Asia, Africa and Latin America, with Thailand helping. Target is 30%+ of revenue from exports by end of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity ramp-up and peak revenue at the new Dahej ethoxylation plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak utilisation is expected about 2 years after commissioning, around end-FY28. The 3x capex-to-peak-sales target is unchanged. Utilisation is about 30% today.

qa_highlights.question: Why did core B2B margin fall YoY, and how will it recover above 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight costs (doubled to tripled) and raw material inflation compressed margins. Some pass-through has been achieved, but freight recovery is still a challenge. No specific recovery date was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Saudi Arabia project timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: The Board approved land leasing in KSA. Feasibility, feedstock and capex work is ongoing, and the next Board approval and detailed timelines are expected in 8-12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Will the gross margin benefit from acquisitions such as Unitop and the move to value-added products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Unitop and Tristar had lower gross margins at acquisition, and in-house ethoxylation now requires advance raw material purchases, which lengthened working capital. Gross margin is better than at end-2021 when the three businesses are combined.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the working capital debt and the net debt trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects working capital debt to be repaid by mid-2027. Net debt fell to Rs 221 crore; H1 operating cash flow was about Rs 131 crore.

risks_watch: Ethylene oxide supply from Reliance is a constraint; the expansion is expected in Q1 FY28, but incremental allocation is not yet confirmed.
Freight and logistics costs are high because of Middle East and Red Sea/Hormuz disruptions, and the core B2B margin fell 70 bps YoY to 14.1%.
The FY27 margin guide of about 12% is below H1 levels of about 12%; the company has not given a clear margin path beyond FY27.
Institutional and B2C is only at breakeven, and plans to sell this business remain undetermined in timing and value.
ROCE has fallen to low teens and is expected to recover only from next year; the Saudi capex return profile is not yet disclosed.
AHN growth has slowed; the seasonal peak in Q3 and Q4 must deliver.

But we don't want to hazard any guess, give anything, which after 6 months, the investors will say, you said it, and you couldn't do it?
So probably next year, we should start seeing improvements in the EBITDA percentage.

543214|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin hit a record 11.90% on INR229.89 crore total income (+19% YoY); order book rose to INR650 crore.
543214|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was INR229.89 crore (+19% YoY), EBITDA INR27.36 crore (+25% YoY) at 11.90% margin, and PAT INR18.45 crore. For FY26, total income was INR825.45 crore (+15%), EBITDA INR93.57 crore (11.34% margin) and PAT INR61.94 crore (+16%). Order book at 31 March 2026 was INR650 crore, up from about INR450 crore at Q3, with the INR200 crore increase entirely from Maruti Suzuki new models. Management declined to give FY27 guidance, instead pointing to a long-term INR3,000 crore revenue ambition for FY30 that is only partly covered by the current order book.

financial_highlights.change: +25% YoY; described as highest ever margin

financial_highlights.metric: ROCE (ex ROU, surplus cash and land)

financial_highlights.change: Revised consolidated cash flow filed 13 May after XBRL filing error
up from about INR450 crore at Q3 FY26; highest in company history

segments.name: Seat covers and frames (NDR Auto)
segments.commentary: NDR does seat covers and frames; Bharat Seats (investee, ~28% held by NDR) does seat assembly and foam. Current revenue run-rate cited as about INR830-850 crore.

segments.name: Hayashi JV (50:50)
segments.commentary: Sunshade business of about INR20 crore transferred to the JV; INR80 crore approved project cost with about INR30 crore invested so far. Production start delayed from April to June due to operational issues. Two small ambient lighting orders from Maruti Suzuki, expected INR10-20 crore revenue combined.

guidance_outlook: No annual guidance given; management pointed to long-term plans. FY30 revenue ambition is INR3,000 crore for NDR standalone (excluding Bharat Seats), implying roughly INR500 crore from existing customers and products plus INR1,000 crore still to be won; updates promised by end of CY2026.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR200 crore order book increase from new models or new OEMs, and what caused the Hayashi JV start delay?

qa_highlights.question: Other expenses rose from INR21 crore to INR24 crore QoQ; were there one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-offs; the rise reflects higher project and marketing expenses including R&D.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 11.5% EBITDA margin sustainable, and what margin range applies as new products ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current margin is sustainable and gave no range for the ramp, citing start-up costs.

qa_highlights.question: How much visibility is there to the INR3,000 crore FY30 target?
qa_highlights.answer: INR500 crore is targeted from existing customers and products; the remaining INR1,000 crore needs more time, with an update promised by end of calendar 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order visibility for the INR150 crore new-product capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Seat belt reminder, seat latch and seat insert orders are already held and will move to the new facilities, with production starting January 2027 and ramping slowly. Hayashi has two ambient lighting orders and the shade business.

qa_highlights.question: Why was operating cash flow weak, and will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said operating cash flow was positive at INR37.12 crore after a corrected filing on 13 May; about INR12 crore went to a Delhi office, INR6 crore supported subsidiaries and MSME vendor payables rose. Management expects normalisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any FY27 revenue or margin guidance?

qa_highlights.question: Capex for FY27 and whether the Bharat Seats target changed?

Medical college plan: about INR 300 crore per 150-seat college, funded through internal accruals, with ROCE above 25-30% indicated; commercial operations expected over the next few years.
Net debt expected to rise marginally by year-end given capex; net debt/EBITDA targeted at 2.5x only if acquisitions are made.

Expansion pipeline: Max Lucknow +100 beds (next two quarters); Sector 56 Gurugram 500 beds phased from end-2026; Nagpur 100 beds and Zirakpur 400 beds in FY28; Pitampura 200 beds in FY29; Patparganj 400 beds by end-FY29; Dwarka 260 beds, Nanavati Phase 2 271 beds and Pune 450 beds by FY30.
capex_capacity: Max Vaishali: board approved INR 425 crore capex for a 202-bed brownfield tower, taking the hospital from 387 beds; construction started and commissioning expected before FY30. Management confirmed this is the same tower previously planned for FY29.
Max Smart: 50% of the 400-bed brownfield tower operational; beds opened are at about 80% occupancy with oncology focus.
Nanavati: remaining 50 beds operational this quarter; Phase 1 beds at about 80% occupancy; Phase 2 (271 beds) to take about 2.5 years and requires shutting about 100 beds.
Network free cash flow INR 397 crore; INR 337 crore invested in ongoing capacity projects and INR 386 crore on acquisitions (Kalinga and Yerawada).
Pune greenfield SPV acquired and now a subsidiary; 450-bed Pune project has IOD and is expected by FY30. Thane and Shaheed Path approvals: 30-36 months delivery after about six months of approvals.
demand_pricing: Occupancy stayed above 75% despite 13% YoY bed capacity growth.
Institutional (CGHS/PSU) share of in-patient revenue fell to 22%, and management said the decline will continue on current infrastructure.
Insurance negotiations ongoing with GIPSA and others; management denied any occupancy impact from insurer pressure on admissions.
Management said CGHS institutional business is loss-making on a fully loaded basis but contributes to fixed costs.
DSO rose to 95 days from 87 days, adding about INR 250 crore of receivables versus Q4 last year, mainly CGHS and PSU collections lumpiness; CGHS new portal is now processing bills.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Parliamentary Standing Committee's healthcare recommendation's impact and any reassessment of expansion plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhay Soi said the report is focused on affordability and that the company is not reassessing expansion; he said any viability issue could become a consolidation opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Will Max Smart and Nanavati beds drive EBITDA quickly given 80% occupancy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA should start rising by the second or third quarter of operations as ARPOB improves after occupancy ramps; Nanavati Phase 1 is already in that curve.

qa_highlights.question: What are the medical college economics and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated INR 300 crore for a 150-seat college, targeting ROCE above 25-30%, starting at Lucknow and funded fully from internal accruals. PG courses are also planned.

qa_highlights.question: Why did FCF grow only 3% when EBITDA grew 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Yogesh Sareen attributed the gap to a receivables build-up (DSO 95 days vs 87), and a higher effective tax rate. FCF conversion was about 56% against the usual 62-65%; he expects normalisation as the new CGHS portal clears bills.

qa_highlights.question: Will oncology and institutional share recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Oncology is expected to normalise from Q3 FY27 and be fully normalised by Q4. Institutional share is expected to keep falling on present infrastructure.

qa_highlights.question: Will opex rise materially before Gurugram comes up?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhay Soi said indirect cost growth came from new capacity at Mohali, Nanavati and Smart plus Bhubaneswar; no major opex increase is expected, so revenue growth should flow to EBITDA.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from new brownfield capacity and Kalinga: EBITDA margin 24.8%, down from 26.8% in Q4 FY26.
Receivables (DSO 95 days) and CGHS collection lumpiness; FCF conversion about 56% vs usual 62-65%.
Kalinga minority shareholder (39% equity, based outside India) litigation over share purchase; company says it has full control.
Net debt up to INR 2,384 crore; management expects it to rise marginally by year-end while capex continues.
Parliamentary Standing Committee's 176th report on affordability and possible FDI caps; no hospital consultations so far.
Insurance renewals in September-October 2026 and whether the 6% automatic price revision holds.
543220|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on capacity ramp-ups, the acquisition playbook and the medical education opportunity. More cautious and deflecting on CGHS economics, receivables and the Kalinga minority shareholder dispute, and it declined to give regional disclosure in the usual form.

543223|2026-03.headline: Max India Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 58% YoY to INR72 crores and quarterly loss narrowed to INR6.8 crores from INR35.5 crores.

Management said the Noida Phase 1 partial occupancy certificate unlocks receivables of over INR150 crores and allows re-filing for Phase 2. Care homes and AGEasy both grew sharply, though care home occupancy averaged lower due to new beds added in Q4. Management is still seeking a fundraise, timing dependent on market conditions.

qa_highlights.question: When will Estate 361 Phase 2 launch, and are residential collections lumpy?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 launch announcement expected within days as 140 of 180 units are sold; collections are lumpy, with booking fee of INR25 lakh, then 10% on application and another 10%, with construction-linked collections over about 3 quarters, lumpy in FY27 and more regular from FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the management fee outlook for E360, E361 and Noida, and the direct cost?

qa_highlights.question: Will Noida Phase 2 start and how much is pending on Phase 1?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 sales expected during FY27 after re-approval of building plans; about 440,000 sq ft remaining. Phase 1 construction complete, with INR70-75 crores of pending bills to be paid.

qa_highlights.question: Why no entry into Hyderabad and what is the status of partnerships?
qa_highlights.answer: Residence entry delayed by unlimited FSI which lets developers maximise density; assisted living in Hyderabad is on the list and to be examined later in FY27. boAt watch product has not taken off as expected, but tech solutions are being worked on; IIT partnership on wheelchairs is a major revenue contributor.

qa_highlights.question: Is AGEasy on track for INR500 crores revenue around FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects continued high growth year-on-year, similar to the past two years, without reiterating the INR500 crore target numerically.

qa_highlights.question: When will the company turn EBITDA and PAT positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to show path to profitability for one or two verticals in later FY27; labour code and minimum wage revisions are a watch item.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of new labour codes and staff costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Labour code impact is about INR3-4 crores across entities, mainly gratuity provisioning, recognised in FY27 as the code came in March 2026. Payroll is about INR80-90 crores; management said the reported top line excludes SPV sales.

qa_highlights.question: When is the fundraise and what about the INR32 crore tax demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Fundraise timing depends on market sentiment; cash comfortable for 3-6 months, with an update expected this year. The INR32 crore tax demand on Dehradun is being contested via rectification for unallowed brought-forward losses; if accepted, it reduces to nil.

qa_highlights.question: Blended ARPOB for Care Homes once occupancy rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said blended ARPOB should be near INR7,500 as recent bed additions were at higher rates.

qa_highlights.question: Bookkeeping: how much of Noida collections is recognised in Q1, and reconciliation of senior living income?
qa_highlights.answer: No Noida revenue was recognised in June; recognition is tied to possession, expected in Q2. qa_highlights.question: Will AGEasy's INR77 crore to about INR150 crore revenue doubling plan hold given Q1 revenue of INR18-19 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the plan; July run-rate reached about INR120 crore annualised, with Q2-Q4 expected to show significant top-line improvement as ROAS improves.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 AGEasy revenue was seasonal, and what are repeat rate and CAC/LTV indicators?

qa_highlights.question: Impact of DLF's senior living entry?

segments.commentary: Dholera multi-integrated facility is expected to be operational in Phase 1 by Q4 FY27, with 2.5 GWh BESS and 100 MW electrolyser Phase 1 capacity. Management guided INR100-200 crore BESS manufacturing business in FY27 as the plant starts only around September-October 2026.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of 40%-plus in FY27, described as conservative by management; it said FY26 growth was about 80%.
FY27 order book targeted at INR1,600-1,650 crore by end of FY27 against an order pipeline of about INR2,000 crore.
Segment mix shifting by about 10 percentage points a year; FY27 targeted at roughly 65:35 (PTS:NRE).
Margin improvement of about 1 percentage point expected in FY27; electrolyser margins 5%-10% initially, rising to about 20% in the subsequent year.
FY27 total capex of INR300-350 crore, including about INR137 crore for PTS/IPP and INR75 crore for BESS and electrolyser subsidiaries; FY26 PTS capex about INR100 crore funded internally.
Fuel cell: technology transfer with AVL and TECO for a plant in Ahmedabad; manual plant in about 1.5 years, automatic in 2-3 years; management sees about 500 MW of fuel cell demand within 2-3 years.
capex_capacity: Solar EPC physical capacity is about 100-200 MW a year, per management, with QRs now in place for large tenders.
Dholera facility: Phase 1 expected operational by Q4 FY27, covering 2.5 GWh BESS and 100 MW electrolyser capacity; BESS plant to be 5 GWh over time.
Electrolyser module range: 250 kW, 500 kW, 1 MW, 2.5 MW and 5 MW single-stack, designed for a 100 MW project.
NABL accreditation received for the existing OPGW, ERS and stringing tools manufacturing facility.
Management expects BESS plant utilisation of 80%-85% in about a year and a half from start.
demand_pricing: Order execution timelines are typically 6 to 18 months depending on business type.

Largest-ever stringing tools and capital tools order of INR22 crore in Q4; ERS supply for MNRE of INR70 crore; first Uttarakhand EPC order of INR33 crore; GETCO re-conductoring EPC order of about INR27 crore.
Management said cost inflation in metals, fuel and other inputs compressed industry margins; conductor and transformer contracts have price-escalation clauses, but OPGW contracts do not.
New ALMM rules for solar from June 1: management said bids already factor them in, the split of government versus private order flow is about 50:50 to 60:40, and it expects limited cell-price impact.
Management expects fuel cell demand to start in FY26 but deliveries from FY27-28; applications are data-centre backup, ferries and defence.

qa_highlights.question: Why is guidance of 40% growth conservative given the INR1,300 crore order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was a little conservative: FY26 growth was about 80% and it expects robust growth in FY27. Order pipeline is about INR2,000 crore, with an FY27-end order book target of INR1,600-1,650 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 BESS revenue INR46 crore if BOO projects will sell electricity?
qa_highlights.answer: The BOO projects were awarded to the group company Advait Green Energy and booked as EPC revenue (INR43 crore). Electricity revenue will sit in SPVs and be consolidated after COD, likely from FY end.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 capex and margin expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed FY27 capex of about INR300-350 crore in total and expects about 1 percentage point of margin improvement in FY27. Electrolyser margins are expected at 5%-10% initially and about 20% in the following year.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company pass on commodity cost inflation to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Conductor and transformer contracts have pass-through clauses; OPGW contracts do not. Management said it has factored these into its bid numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Why were four subsidiaries created, and who holds the other 20% of one of them?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidiaries were set up for focused growth, bank facilities and future equity raises, with AGPL for electrolysers and solar EPC, the battery company for BESS and C&I, Akara for carbon and Aura for assets. The 20% holder was not answered on the call and was deferred to email.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company fund capex and what about dilution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said funding will use both equity and debt in a mix based on business composition, and equity dilution would happen only if it benefits shareholders. No quantum was given.

qa_highlights.question: When will the company move to pure-play solar EPC and what is the solar EPC capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to bid on large tenders including module-supply projects and win some orders this year. Physical capacity is about 100-200 MW a year.

risks_watch: Operating cash flow was about INR5.8 crore against PAT of INR58 crore in FY26; management attributed this to working capital build-up from the Q4 revenue surge and gave no timeline for conversion.
Debt-equity rose to 0.46x from 0.23x, and management said further capex will need a mix of equity dilution and debt; no quantum was disclosed.
Margin pressure from metal and fuel cost inflation and from the NRE mix shift; Q4 consolidated EBITDA margin of 12.61% compares with 11.73% for FY26 and 12.87% in FY25.
Electrolyser and fuel cell timelines depend on government policy and market opening; the Dholera facility is due Q4 FY27 and fuel cell deliveries from FY27-28.
Ownership structure of the 80% subsidiary (Advait Carbon) was not clarified on the call.

Some answers were inconsistent: management cited Q4 standalone PAT as rising from INR15 crore to INR10 crore, and the Dholera BESS plant start timeline (Q4 FY27 versus September-October 2026) was not fully reconciled.
543230|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and expansive on the long-term energy transition story and order book, but evasive on specifics such as subsidiary ownership, funding quantum and fuel cell revenue. Management called its own FY27 growth guidance conservative, while acknowledging margin pressure from input costs.

543230|2026-09.headline: Advait Energy Q2 FY27 revenue rose 40.8% YoY to INR 221 crore, with EBITDA margin at 14.5% and order book at INR 1,575 crore.
543230|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 221 crore (up 40.8% YoY), EBITDA INR 32 crore (up 84.4%) and PAT INR 19 crore (up 88.5%). H1 FY27 revenue was INR 400 crore (up 45.4%) with PAT of INR 34 crore. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth of 55-60% (above INR 1,000 crore) and a long-term INR 5,000 crore revenue ambition. Debt-to-equity rose to 0.86x from 0.42x at March 2026, and an equity raise is planned for Q3 or Q4 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +84.4% YoY; margin vs 11% in Q2 FY26
+88.5% YoY vs INR 10 crore; margin vs 6.5%
+77.9% YoY vs INR 19 crore; margin vs 6.9%

financial_highlights.metric: Order book (incl. L1) as on 30 Sep 2026

segments.name: Power Transmission Solutions (PTS)
segments.commentary: Order book mix about 60-65% PTS vs 35% NRE; PTS EBITDA margin described as steady over four years. Recent orders include about INR 52 crore from DGVCL and multiple PGVCL orders, plus ERS, OPGW and stringing tools.

segments.name: New & Renewable Energy (NRE)
segments.commentary: Management guides NRE EBITDA margin of 7-8% to build 30-50% over two years, driven by manufacturing. Current solar and green hydrogen EPC margins are cited at 5-8%; a 150 MW / 300 MWh standalone BESS order in Junagadh, Gujarat was secured. A 100 MW solar EPC order from KP Group targets 8-10% EBITDA.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of 55-60% YoY, crossing INR 1,000 crore; H2 FY27 needs about INR 700 crore (about INR 325-350 crore per quarter), which management says is on track.

Group EBITDA margin: management says it is looking for similar levels to H1 (about 14%) in H2 FY27, but declined to use the word 'committing'; group margin targeted at 15% once manufacturing is established, with 1-1.5% annual improvement meanwhile.

Long-term: INR 5,000 crore revenue target over about 5 years; manufacturing share of sales targeted at 70-75% by FY28-29 (other comment: 65-75% by FY28-29/FY29-30); NRE and PTS targeted at roughly 50:50 contribution in 2-3 years.
Capex: FY27 guidance of INR 300-350 crore; INR 101 crore incurred in H1 and about INR 140 crore planned in H2.
Target debt-to-equity for manufacturing and solutions business of about 0.5-0.7x; equity raise planned for Q3 or Q4 FY27 to fund working capital.
capex_capacity: Gangad, Gujarat integrated manufacturing facility: Phase 1 operational by Q4 FY27 across PTS and NRE.
2.5 GWh BESS manufacturing facility (expandable to 5 GWh): final plant and machinery orders placed; operational by Q4 FY27. Management guides 40-60% utilisation in year one.

Electrolyser: 30 MW assembly line inaugurated March 2026; first 1 MW unit being assembled in-house for engineering development. Management plans 150 MW operational around Q4 FY27 (within a 300 MW Phase 2), with capacity expandable to 1 GW by 2028-29.
Completed electrolyser projects: 300 kW for THDC (Rishikesh) and a 1 MW EPC and supply project in Gujarat, expected to be commissioned in the current quarter.
Fuel cell: INR 22 crore investment linked to a technology licence with AVL and TECO; management promised a sizeable update next quarter, including a timeline for the first plant.
demand_pricing: Order book split about 60-65% public and 40% private; management says collection cycles in public and private have been equally efficient.
Order book mix by execution: about 60-62% EPC and about 38% manufacturing; target 70-75% manufacturing from FY28-29.
New order inflow for next year expected 50:50 PTS and NRE; management expects order book at least 1.6-1.8x last year's revenue.

Revenue potential: 150 MW electrolyser capacity cited at INR 600-1,000 crore; BESS at about INR 1,000-1,100 crore per GWh at full utilisation. PTS full-capacity manufacturing sales above INR 2,500 crore.

Management said over 13 Indian green hydrogen players engaged through the 5 MW live testing programme and cited an active electrolyser inquiry pipeline above 1 GW. It also said Chinese equipment is excluded from public tenders and some Japan/Europe-backed projects.

qa_highlights.question: What gives conviction in the INR 5,000 crore revenue target over about 5 years (about 7x FY26)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 50-60% revenue and EBITDA CAGR over the past 6-7 years and said the company is now qualified for larger product and project sizes; it did not break down the drivers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the public vs private mix in the INR 1,575 crore order book and how does it affect collections?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly 60-65% public and 40% private; collection cycles in public have been as efficient as private over the last 3-4 years. Exact figures to follow via CFO.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PTS margin fall while NRE margin rose?
qa_highlights.answer: PTS margin has been steady for four years with about 1.5% annual change; NRE margin is improving and is guided up 30-50% over two years, driven by manufacturing and solutions.

qa_highlights.question: Explain the INR 22 crore TECO investment and its status, given TECO's reported bankruptcy filing.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a licence-linked investment for fuel cell technology with AVL and TECO for about a decade, not an equity stake in the company. It promised an update next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Ind-AS 115 adjusted core revenue and EBITDA, and the gap between NRE revenue of about INR 4 crore and EBIT of INR 7.8 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Core manufacturing EBITDA is 17-18% standalone; NRE EPC EBITDA is 5-7%. Management said the operating profit is from operational revenue only, with margins varying order to order (6-8%). No reconciliation was provided.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance of INR 1,100 crore and the 14% margin still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the track is in line, with H2 growth of 55-60%, and that inflation was partly covered by pre-booked raw materials. It would not call 14% a commitment, but expects similar numbers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt and capital structure plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Target D/E of 0.5-0.7x for the manufacturing and solutions business; asset-creation business model may shift leverage. Equity raise planned for Q3 or Q4 FY27 for working capital.

qa_highlights.question: What is the electrolyser order pipeline and when does the 300 MW Phase 2 come on stream?
qa_highlights.answer: No electrolyser orders yet booked from the 30 MW line; 150 MW expected operational around Q4 FY27 given an active inquiry above 1 GW, with orders above 150 MW targeted for FY27-28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost basis of the AGPL share purchase (INR 6,250 vs INR 25,000 per share)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give the figure and referred the question to the CFO by email. AGPL requires funding backed by AETL.

qa_highlights.question: What is expected utilisation and revenue for the 2.5 GWh BESS plant, and how does it reconcile with the INR 5,000 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Year-one utilisation of 40-60%, with the mix of captive and open-market orders not split. Management said the INR 5,000 crore target is the base case and that capital allocation and cash flow will set the pace.

risks_watch: Electrolyser: the 30 MW line had no booked orders as of the call; the 150 MW Q4 FY27 start depends on converting a >1 GW inquiry pipeline.
Balance sheet: D/E rose to 0.86x from 0.42x, and borrowings of INR 280 crore; the planned equity raise in Q3 or Q4 FY27 is pending.
Margin: H2 inflation risk to the 14% EBITDA margin; NRE EPC margins of 5-8% are well below the core manufacturing 17-18%.
Execution: H1 executed orders of about INR 400 crore against a H2 requirement of about INR 700 crore to reach INR 1,100 crore.
Disclosure gaps: no exact order-book product split, no AGPL deal value, no reconciliation of NRE revenue vs EBIT, and the TECO investment remains unclear.
543230|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth and the manufacturing transition, but evasive on several specifics: it deferred exact order-book splits, the AGPL deal value and the NRE revenue/EBIT gap to email follow-up, and declined to commit to the 14% margin.
key_quotes: Broadly, I can tell you our debt-to-equity ratio for our manufacturing and solution business will be about 0.5x to 0.7x.
So we are looking forward to have similar numbers.
We are not looking forward to put out the entire 300-MW capacity to be operational in 2027.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Gangad Phase 1 (PTS and NRE), 2.5 GWh BESS plant (plant and machinery orders placed) and 150 MW electrolyser within Phase 2 are all guided operational around Q4 FY27, with capex of INR 140 crore planned in H2 FY27 against INR 101 crore spent in H1.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth of 55-60% (above INR 1,000 crore) reiterated, needing about INR 700 crore in H2 (INR 325-350 crore per quarter) versus INR 400 crore in H1; order book about INR 1,575 crore, up 47% YoY, with execution described as on track.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex guided at INR 300-350 crore with INR 140 crore planned in H2, and a fuel cell update with a first-plant timeline promised next quarter; the INR 22 crore fuel cell investment is licence-linked and the capex plan is already set.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is reiterating rather than raising FY27 growth of 55-60%, and the H2 requirement of about INR 700 crore is already a stretch against H1 of INR 400 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Fuel cell technology update with a first-plant timeline promised next quarter, and the 150 MW electrolyser and 2.5 GWh BESS start-ups are guided for Q4 FY27; the 1 MW in-house unit is already being assembled.

rows.label: Electrolyser order conversion from >1 GW inquiry pipeline
rows.why: No electrolyser orders yet booked from the 30 MW line, while 150 MW is targeted around Q4 FY27 and orders above 150 MW are targeted for FY27-28 against a pipeline above 1 GW.

rows.why: Equity raise is planned to fund working capital as D/E rose to 0.86x from 0.42x on INR 280 crore gross borrowings, against a target of 0.5-0.7x for the manufacturing business.

rows.label: NRE margin ramp to 30-50% over two years
rows.why: NRE EPC margins are 5-8% today, with a 100 MW KP Group solar EPC order targeting 8-10% EBITDA; the ramp depends on manufacturing coming online.

543232|2026-03.headline: CAMS Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record with non-MF revenue up ~24.5% YoY and EBITDA margin back at ~46.5%, while MF revenue was flat (+0.5% QoQ).
543232|2026-03.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue and absolute EBITDA of about INR183 crores, with margin recovering to about 46.5% from 45% a year earlier. Non-MF revenue grew about 24.5% YoY and now contributes about 15.3% of enterprise revenue, with non-MF EBITDA margin above 16%. MF revenue was nearly flat, with AUM at INR55.1 lakh crores (down from INR58.5 lakh crores at one point in Q4 on Middle East-related market weakness) but up 21% YoY. Management guided to sub-5% employee cost growth and sub-9% total expense growth in FY27, flat KRA revenue, and at least 20% non-MF growth.

financial_highlights.value: ~24.5% of growth YoY; 15.3% share of enterprise revenue

financial_highlights.change: Up from ~INR177 crores QoQ; ~INR173-174 crores peak in prior-year Q4

financial_highlights.value: ~9% YoY incl. depreciation; ~7.8% excl. depreciation; <1.5% QoQ
INR 4 per share (subject to shareholder approval); total FY26 payout ~INR305 crores
Just over INR1 lakh crore; CAMS share 76% (from 71% in prior quarter)
Almost INR59,000 crore in quarter; crossed INR20,000 crore in March
financial_highlights.change: +17% YoY vs industry +4%; collection share 57% to 64%

financial_highlights.value: AUM above INR3 lakh crore; 50% outsourced share
Revenue +28% YoY for quarter; KRA non-MF share ~30%

segments.name: Mutual fund (RTA/core)
segments.commentary: Revenue almost flat (~+0.5% YoY); AUM INR55.1 lakh crore, up 21% YoY with 68% overall share; yields stable, QoQ compression under 1% attributed to passive mix shift. Headcount in core MF operations reduced by ~70 YoY.

segments.name: Non-MF (overall)
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~24.5% YoY, broad-based across CAMSPay, AIF, KRA; FY26 non-MF growth ~18% due to weak Q1. Non-MF EBITDA margin upwards of 16%, targeting 20% by end FY27.

segments.name: CAMSPay (payments)
segments.commentary: Payment aggregator (PA) and payment gateway (PG) both grew ~23% YoY; cards business ~25% of quarterly revenue, all non-MF; non-MF now above 50% of CAMSPay revenue.

segments.name: KRA
segments.commentary: Revenue +28% YoY despite demat/broking slowdown; NSE KRA integration added ~13-14 lakh PANs. Industry-wide ~20% fee cut from 1 April 2026 expected to reduce revenue by INR8 crore, offset by INR3 crore NSE KRA uplift; management guides flat FY27 revenue.

segments.name: Alternatives (AIF)
segments.commentary: Revenue +25% YoY; AUM crossed INR3 lakh crore; 44 new full-service mandates incl. 14 new logos; 50% share of outsourced market.

segments.name: Repository / Insurance and others
segments.commentary: Rep revenue +6% YoY. Bima Central active users doubled; LIC started demat-format policy issuance. IR market share expanded to 40%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 employee cost growth guided below 5%; total expense growth guided below 9%, with a stated aim to be lower; increments effective from Q2 FY27.

Management aims to retain Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin (~46.5%) through FY27 after absorbing salary increases, investments and yield compression; no formal margin range given (bad quarter below 45%, good quarter ~46-47%).
Non-MF revenue growth of at least 20% in FY27 (~INR45-50 crore incremental on a ~INR250 crore base), with payments ~INR20 crore, AIF ~INR7-8 crore, Rep ~INR7-8 crore, AA/TSP/pension ~INR15 crore.
KRA revenue guided flat in FY27 after ~INR8 crore price-cut impact offset by ~INR3 crore NSE KRA uplift and new-logo growth.
MF yield decline expected to be less than 3% (historical 3-3.5%); target 20% non-MF EBITDA margin by end of next year.
Revenue expected to grow on flat-to-falling headcount in FY27; ReArch expected to be a 5-year program, about 2 years done, ~3-4% behind schedule curve.
capex_capacity: ReArch cloud-native platform: 9 significant modules; transaction origination module fully built and launching to several thousand integrators; data lake (on Google Cloud BigQuery) to go live in 1H FY27; data warehouse and next-gen transaction origination platform ready within 3-4 months.
Team of close to 200 engineers on ReArch; headcount at FY26 end 8,420 vs 8,324 at FY25 end (ReArch hires >100; core MF headcount reduced ~70).
Form data extraction now runs in production with maker step removed (AI performs data entry; physical checker retained), ~1 million physical forms per month.
SIFs: 6 live as of Q4 FY26 after 4 launches in the quarter; ~8 more licensed or announced, with launches expected May-August 2026.

ConsenPro (DPDP compliance product, built in Think360) launched commercially; ~40,000-50,000 Indian companies expected to need it over 1.5 years. Unified device product (payments and KYC) noted as an adjacency.
demand_pricing: Industry-wide KRA fee cut of ~20% effective 1 April 2026, voluntary and coordinated; KRA base ~INR42-43 crore for FY27.
MF yield compression QoQ under 1%, attributed to passives mix (passives under 10% of AUM); management says no yield cut in individual asset classes. Equity share of AUM ~54-55%.
Mid-sized AMC contract renewals due during FY27; management does not expect material yield decline; a possible 3-5 bps AMC-level pass-through discussed but no concrete RTA fee change agreed.
Licensed domestic AMCs at 31; new AMCs (e.g., Neo, Oaklane) onboarded on scale-play logic. Management says it is selling value rather than price.
IR market share 40%; KRA now number 2 in KRA market after gaining share over ~1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Opex growth of ~10% in FY26 is the lowest in 5 years: how much is deliberate discretionary cost management versus sustainable savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Ram Charan said the cost actions are structural and automation-led, not a one-off squeeze. Headcount rose ~100-120 people YoY, with ReArch hiring offset by a ~70 reduction in core MF operations. Total cost growth was 9% including depreciation and 7.8% excluding it, with QoQ cost growth under 1.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Passive mix shift typically hurts RTA yields more than AMC yields. Is there scope to renegotiate RTA pricing on passives or to gain bargaining power on the active book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said passives are under 10% of AUM and already priced at very low levels, so there is no room to renegotiate. Yield compression QoQ (<1%) came from mix, not from lower rates in any asset class. Ram Charan said the mix shift is an argument to raise with AMCs, but it is not a decisive one.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 3-5 bps AMC fee cut be passed to RTA fees? Is any RTA fee negotiation under way?
qa_highlights.answer: No concrete RTA fee change has been agreed. Discussions may happen, but management said it is comfortable with the price-value equation and does not expect a material impact.

qa_highlights.question: Should yield decline be modelled at the historical 3-3.5% for FY27 and FY28, given that margins have previously dropped from 46-47% to 42-44%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 3-3.5% is the 5-year average and should be used as a conservative model input, with the aim being a lower number, possibly under 3%. On margins, Anuj Kumar said 46% was reached about 5 quarters ago, dropped to 42%, and has now been regained over 4 quarters. He attributed the earlier fall to investments in non-revenue businesses made over 2022-2025.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 guidance for employee cost, overall expenses and EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost growth is guided below 5% and total expense growth below 9%, with increments effective from Q2 FY27. No formal margin guidance was given; the aim is to retain the Q4 FY26 margin of ~46.5% after salary increases, investments and yield compression.

qa_highlights.question: How will the ~20% non-MF growth be built in FY27 with KRA flat, and what is the breakdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a base of ~INR60-62 crore quarterly non-MF revenue, or ~INR250 crore annualised. It needs ~INR45-50 crore of increment: payments ~INR20 crore, AIF ~INR7-8 crore, Rep ~INR7-8 crore, AA/TSP/pension ~INR15 crore (quoted as INR4-5 crore in one place and ~INR15 crore in another), with ConsenPro and GIFT City adding a few crore.

qa_highlights.question: KRA: what is the price cut, and how is FY27 revenue flat after it?
qa_highlights.answer: The industry-wide ~20% fee cut from 1 April 2026 is expected to reduce KRA revenue by ~INR8 crore on a base of ~INR42-43 crore. NSE KRA integration adds ~INR3 crore, leaving a ~INR5 crore gap that management expects to close through new-logo growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is ConsenPro and what is the market opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: ConsenPro is a commercial DPDP-compliance product built inside Think360 from an internal captive offering. It covers consent management, data discovery, regulatory reporting and consulting. Management expects ~40,000-50,000 Indian companies to need it over ~1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Could a single KYC regime through CKYC reduce KRA pricing or volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CKYC is not yet eligible to substitute for KRA KYC. KRA runs a second verification layer (name match, face match, DOB and address against DigiLocker or UIDAI), so the risk is seen as a watch item rather than an immediate threat.

risks_watch: MF yield: the passive mix shift continues to pull yields down. Any AMC pass-through of 3-5 bps could lead to RTA fee discussions. Management guides yield decline below 3%, against a 3-3.5% historical average, and says no concrete RTA fee change has been agreed.

KRA: a ~INR8 crore fee cut from 1 April 2026 is only partly offset by ~INR3 crore from NSE KRA. FY27 flat guidance depends on new-logo growth to fill a ~INR5 crore gap. A possible single-KYC/CKYC shift is a watch item.

Margin sustainability: management is targeting retention of the ~46.5% Q4 margin through FY27 after salary increases, investments and yield compression. Past cycles show margins falling back to 42-44% after investment phases.

MF AUM and asset growth: AUM fell from INR58.5 lakh crore at a point in Q4 to INR55.1 lakh crore, reflecting Middle East-related market weakness. Management says asset growth is awaited after the last two months, and FY27 MF revenue is not guided.

ReArch execution: a 5-year programme with ~2 years done and ~3-4% behind the schedule curve. The data lake is due in 1H FY27, and the data warehouse and next-gen transaction origination platform are due within 3-4 months. Non-MF margin target is 20% by end FY27.

Non-MF growth dependence: ~20% FY27 growth needs ~INR45-50 crore of incremental revenue. The breakdown includes ~INR20 crore from payments, with a new-logo pipeline (SIFs, ConsenPro, GIFT City) still early.
